### Commercial and Financial Summary of Pompeian, Inc.

#### Company Overview
Pompeian, Inc., founded in 1906 and based in Baltimore, is a leading producer and distributor of olive oil and other related products in the United States. Initially established in Italy, the company moved its production to the U.S. due to market demand and strategic growth. Pompeian is known for its high-quality olive oils, which include extra virgin, organic, and light-tasting varieties. Over the years, Pompeian has expanded its product line to include vinegars and cooking sprays, maintaining a strong market presence as America's largest importer of olive oil.

#### Products and Market Position
- **Olive Oils**: Pompeian's olive oils are crafted from carefully selected olives, ensuring premium quality and taste. Their product range includes robust, smooth, and organic extra virgin olive oils, suitable for various culinary applications from sautéing to drizzling.
- **Grapeseed Oil**: Known for its high smoke point, Pompeian's grapeseed oil is ideal for high-heat cooking. It is rich in Vitamin E and essential fatty acids.
- **Vinegars**: Pompeian offers a range of gourmet vinegars, including organic options, that pair well with their olive oils.
- **Cooking Sprays**: These sprays come in various types such as grapeseed oil, organic robust EVOO, coconut oil, and avocado oil. The unique can-and-pouch system ensures no propellants or artificial additives are mixed with the oil.

#### Financial Performance
- **Revenue**: Pompeian's annual revenue ranges between $100 million and $500 million, reflecting its strong market position and consistent growth.
- **Ownership**: The company is privately held, with significant investments from the Devico family and a strategic partnership with the DCOOP Group of Spain. This partnership has bolstered Pompeian's production capabilities and market reach.

#### Strategic Initiatives and Community Engagement
- **Sustainability**: Pompeian is dedicated to sustainable practices, exemplified by their Sustainably Grown® Certified Olive Farm initiative.
- **Community Support**: The company actively supports local communities through donations and involvement in educational programs, exemplified by their contributions to the Baltimore City Public School System and other local institutions.

Pompeian continues to innovate and expand its product offerings while maintaining a commitment to quality and sustainability, ensuring its position as a leader in the olive oil market in the United States.

For more detailed information, visit their [official website](https://pompeian.com/)【17†source】【18†source】.

To estimate the length of a vessel based on its TEU capacity, we typically consider the vessel's design, which includes factors such as the number of container bays, the length of the ship's hull, and the arrangement of containers on deck.

For a rough estimate, we can use industry standards and data from similar vessels. A 5000 TEU vessel would likely have a length of around 300 to 350 meters (about 984 to 1148 feet). However, the actual length can vary depending on the specific design and configuration of the ship.

TEU stands for "Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit." It's a standard measure in the container shipping industry used to describe the capacity of container ships and container terminals. One TEU is equal to the volume of a standard 20-foot-long shipping container. So, when you hear that a ship has a capacity of, for example, 5,000 TEUs, it means it can carry 5,000 standard 20-foot containers.

To estimate the length of a 5000 TEU vessel, we need to consider that TEU stands for "Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit," meaning it's based on the size of a standard 20-foot-long shipping container. However, ships can accommodate containers of varying lengths, including 20 feet, 40 feet, and even 45 feet.

A rough estimate would be to assume that the average length of a TEU container is about 20 feet. So, for a 5000 TEU vessel:

5000 TEUs * 20 feet per TEU = 100,000 feet

This gives us the total length of containers that the vessel can carry. However, we also need to account for the space between containers, the ship's infrastructure, and other factors.

The Westervelt Company today announced that President and CEO Brian Luoma will retire at the end of 2023. Luoma joined Westervelt in 2017, and his tenure has been marked by growth of the company, most notably the expansion of the Lumber business through the construction of a new lumber mill in Thomasville, Alabama.

Cade Warner, Chief Operating Officer, has been selected to succeed Luoma and was recently appointed to the Board of Directors. He joined Westervelt in 2017 and has held roles in strategy and planning, sustainability and continuous improvement.

“We have been working toward this transition for some time, and both Brian and Cade have created an opportunity for a seamless shift in leadership,” said Rob Taylor, Chairman of the Board. “Brian has done an excellent job leading the Company, especially during the uncertainty of the pandemic years, and we appreciate his dedication to growing the company and the capability of our employees. We are eager to welcome Cade to the Board and into his new role. His experience and passion for this industry will be essential in continuing to guide the growth of the Company.”

“When I joined Westervelt, I found a company loaded with talent,” said Luoma. “I am very proud of everything we accomplished as a team, particularly the continued development of our people and their relentless commitment to our customers and the quality of our products and services. Throughout the remainder of this year, Cade and I will continue to work closely together as we transition leadership. Sustainability has been a core value for Westervelt for more than a century, and it will continue to expand under Cade’s leadership. I am very excited to see what the future holds for Cade and the next generation of leaders at The Westervelt Company.”

About The Westervelt Company

The Westervelt Company, a privately held company headquartered in Tuscaloosa, Ala., was founded in 1884 and is currently under the fourth generation of family leadership. Westervelt is an industry leader in land management, wood products manufacturing and environmental mitigation. The company is recognized for excellence in sustainable forest management, responsibly sourced forest products and services, natural resource stewardship and ecosystem conservation. With more than half a million acres of land under Westervelt management, Westervelt’s diverse businesses all work together to ensure the sustainable stewardship of natural resources today, tomorrow and for many generations to come.

To assess the potential return on investment (ROI) for establishing a data center in an emerging Southeast Asian market, let's consider the Philippines as our hypothetical case. This choice is driven by its growing status as a preferred destination for data center construction due to the spillover demand from nearby markets like Singapore【26†source】.

### Initial Setup and Running Costs
1. **Capital Expenditure (CapEx)**:
   - **Land Acquisition and Construction**: Costs would vary significantly depending on the location within the Philippines. Urban areas like Manila might have higher land and construction costs compared to rural areas.
   - **Equipment**: Essential data center equipment includes servers, cooling systems, power supplies, and security measures.

2. **Operational Expenditure (OpEx)**:
   - **Energy Costs**: The Philippines has relatively high electricity costs, which could impact long-term operational budgets.
   - **Staffing and Maintenance**: Local labor costs are generally lower than in more developed markets, which might reduce the operational expenditure.

### Revenue Potential
- **Service Demand**: There's a growing demand for cloud services and data storage in the Philippines, driven by increasing digitalization in both the private and public sectors. The adoption of cloud-based services and the necessity for local data storage due to data localization laws are significant drivers【26†source】.

### ROI Calculation
- **Breakeven Analysis**: It would be essential to calculate how long it would take for the initial investments to be recouped through operational revenues. This depends on the pricing strategy for the services offered and the occupancy rate of the data center.
- **Growth Prospects**: The data center market in Southeast Asia is expected to grow at a CAGR of 6.57%, reaching a market volume of $14.19 billion by 2028【26†source】. This growth rate suggests a promising return on investment if the data center meets regional demand effectively.

### Risk Factors
- **Regulatory Risks**: Changes in local laws regarding foreign ownership and data sovereignty could impact operations.
- **Market Competition**: Increased competition from local and international players can affect pricing and market share.
- **Technological Obsolescence**: Rapid changes in technology require continuous investments to keep the data center up-to-date.

### Conclusion
Investing in a data center in the Philippines could be financially viable given the region's growth trajectory and digitalization initiatives. However, a detailed financial model incorporating specific local data on costs, demand, and competitive landscape would be crucial for a more accurate ROI calculation and risk assessment. This strategic move should align with broader corporate objectives, considering both financial returns and strategic positioning in a growing market.

metadata.text:
* Several operators are signing power purchase agreements to adopt green energy sources for their operations. For instance, Facebook has signed a power purchase agreement with Sunseap Group under which Sunseap Group will provide renewable energy to the Singapore facility of Facebook. 
  * In November 2021, PLDT partnered with Mpower to power its VITRO's data center in the Philippines via renewable energy, which will support the government's aim to achieve an energy mix of 50% by 2040. The company has signed a deal to provide 1,500 MW for five to seven years. 
  * Several countries are witnessing microgrids' establishment that will further aid in adopting greener energy sources. For instance, SP Group has announced investments for microgrid establishment at the Singapore Institute of Technology campus. 

SUPPLY & DEMAND IN SOUTHEAST ASIA DATA CENTER MARKET

  * On average, the occupancy rate of data centers across Southeast Asia is 60-70%; Singapore is the leading country with occupancy of over 85%. 
  * In 2020, the moratorium on data center investments in Singapore aided the strong growth of data center demand across Indonesia, Malaysia, and other countries. 
  * The expansion of cloud regions by hyperscale cloud service providers and internet service providers is fuelling the major demand for services in the region. 
  * Most of the new announcements are focused on hyperscale development with a full-built capacity of over 20 MW or edge data center facilities. 
  * On-premise data center operations are higher in sectors such as BFSI, government agencies, and education institutions. 
  * Local telecommunication providers offering data center services will face severe competition through the entry of multiple operators into the regions. 
  * The market is witnessing the entry of several new entrants, such as OneAsia Network, Pure Data Centers, Nautilus Data Technologies, SC Zeus, EdgeConneX, Edge Centres, ESR Cayman, GDS Services, and Yondr.

Yes, accessible data centers are indeed a bottleneck in some parts of the world. This limitation can significantly impact the deployment and effectiveness of advanced technologies like cloud computing and edge computing, particularly in the following areas:

1. **Remote and Rural Areas**: In many parts of the world, especially in less developed or geographically isolated regions, the infrastructure needed to support data centers—such as reliable electricity, high-speed internet connections, and secure facilities—is often lacking.

2. **Developing Countries**: Many developing countries face challenges related to power reliability, bandwidth availability, and political stability, which can hinder the establishment and maintenance of data centers. 

3. **High-Cost Regions**: In some high-cost regions, the economic feasibility of operating data centers due to high land prices, energy costs, and regulatory compliance can be prohibitive. This makes it difficult for companies to justify the investment unless there is substantial demand.

4. **Regions with Harsh Environmental Conditions**: Areas with extreme weather conditions (too hot, too cold, or prone to natural disasters) pose significant challenges for maintaining the operational integrity and efficiency of data centers.

5. **Regions with Strict Data Sovereignty Laws**: Countries with stringent data sovereignty or localization laws require data to be stored within national borders, potentially necessitating local data centers. This can be a bottleneck if local infrastructure is inadequate.

Investing in technologies that mitigate these limitations, such as developing more robust and efficient edge computing solutions that require less centralized data processing, or using renewable energy sources to power data centers, can be particularly strategic. These investments not only address the bottleneck but also align well with global trends towards sustainability and decentralized data processing.

Evaluating the return on investment (ROI) for data center projects, especially in regions where access to such facilities is a bottleneck, involves a multi-faceted analysis. Here are the key factors to consider and the steps to estimate the potential ROI:

### 1. **Initial and Ongoing Costs**
   - **Capital Expenditure (CapEx)**: Includes the cost of purchasing land, construction, and the necessary equipment like servers, cooling systems, and security measures.
   - **Operational Expenditure (OpEx)**: Ongoing costs such as energy consumption, maintenance, staff salaries, and regular upgrades.

### 2. **Revenue Streams**
   - **Direct Revenue**: From clients who rent server space, use your cloud services, or leverage your data processing capabilities.
   - **Indirect Revenue**: Enhanced business operations leading to cost savings in other areas of the company, such as improved logistics efficiency or faster customer service response times.

### 3. **Cost Savings and Efficiency Gains**
   - **Energy Efficiency**: Modern data centers can be designed with energy-efficient technologies that minimize operational costs.
   - **Reduced Downtime**: Improved reliability and uptime can lead to higher customer satisfaction and retention.

### 4. **Compliance and Risk Mitigation**
   - **Data Sovereignty Compliance**: Helps avoid fines and legal issues by complying with local data laws, which could be financially beneficial depending on the penalties for non-compliance.
   - **Disaster Recovery**: Having robust data centers can mitigate the risks and potential costs associated with data loss or system downtime.

### 5. **Market Growth Potential**
   - **Expansion into New Markets**: Entering underserved markets can provide new revenue opportunities and increase market share.
   - **First-Mover Advantage**: Establishing infrastructure in emerging markets can position your company as a leader in those regions, potentially leading to greater long-term profits.

### Steps to Calculate ROI
1. **Estimate Total Costs**: Sum up all initial CapEx and projected OpEx for a defined period (e.g., 5-10 years).

To truly free up space, you need to delete emails. Here are some steps to help you free up space more effectively:

1. **Find Large Emails**:
   - In the Gmail search bar, type `has:attachment larger:10M` to find emails with attachments larger than 10MB.
2. **Select and Delete**:
   - Select these emails and delete them.

### Emptying Trash and Spam
1. **Empty Trash**:
   - Go to the Trash folder.
   - Click on "Empty Trash now".
2. **Empty Spam**:
   - Go to the Spam folder.
   - Click on "Delete all spam messages now".

### Managing Storage with Google One
1. **Check Storage Usage**:
   - Visit [Google One Storage](https://one.google.com/storage) to see a breakdown of your storage usage.
2. **Remove Unwanted Files**:
   - Follow the recommendations provided by Google One to delete large files and emails.

To efficiently archive all your emails in Gmail and free up space, you can follow these steps:

### Method 1: Using Gmail's Archive Function
1. **Open Gmail**: Log in to your Gmail account.
2. **Select All Emails**: 
   - Go to the inbox or any label containing emails you want to archive.
   - Check the box at the top left to select all emails on the page.
   - Click the "Select all conversations" link that appears to select all emails in that category.
3. **Archive Emails**: Click the "Archive" button (a box with a downward arrow).

### Method 2: Using Google Takeout
1. **Access Google Takeout**:
   - Go to [Google Takeout](https://takeout.google.com/settings/takeout).
2. **Select Data to Export**:
   - Deselect all, then scroll down to select "Mail".
3. **Choose File Type and Size**:
   - Choose your preferred file type and size. (Default is usually fine.)
4. **Create Export**:
   - Click on "Create export". This will download a copy of your emails.
5. **Delete Emails from Gmail**:
   - After confirming your emails are safely exported, return to Gmail.
   - Use the search bar to select all emails (e.g., using `in:all`).
   - Delete them to free up space.

### Method 3: Using an Email Client (e.g., Outlook, Thunderbird)
1. **Set Up the Email Client**:
   - Download and install an email client like Outlook or Thunderbird.
   - Add your Gmail account using IMAP settings.
2. **Download Emails**:
   - Let the client download all your emails.
3. **Archive Locally**:
   - Use the client's archive function to move emails to local folders.
4. **Delete Emails from Gmail**:
   - After ensuring your emails are saved locally, delete them from Gmail.

Carbohydrate Solutions Summary

Carbohydrate Solutions segment operating profit was $309 million during the fourth quarter of 2023, up 12% compared to the prior year period. The Starches & Sweeteners sub-segment increased $9 million, as higher pricing and lower input costs offset headwinds from lower volumes and co-product margins. In Vantage Corn Processing (VCP), results improved $23 million as strong export demand and steady domestic blending supported margins and higher ethanol production. 

For the full year, Carbohydrate Solutions segment operating profit was $1,375 million, 3% lower versus the prior year. Higher starches & sweeteners pricing and mix were offset by weaker volumes and cycling one-time benefits in 2022 of $50 million related to USDA Biofuel Producer Recovery Program in VCP.

Nutrition Summary

Nutrition segment operating profit was negative $10 million during the fourth quarter of 2023, down 110% compared to the prior year period. Human Nutrition segment operating profit was negative $25 million, approximately $112 million lower versus the prior year period, as operational challenges led to lower volumes and increased manufacturing costs. The quarter also included negative impacts of $64 million related to deconsolidation and write-down of a joint venture, and an investment valuation loss. Unplanned downtime at Decatur East was also a negative impact. Animal Nutrition operating profit of $15 million was 17% lower versus the prior year, driven largely by lower amino acid margins and lower sub-segment volumes overall. 

For the full year, Nutrition segment operating profit was $427 million, 36% lower versus the prior year. Human Nutrition results of $417 million were 25% lower than the prior year, as higher pricing was more than offset by weaker volumes and increased costs. The full year also included negative impacts of $64 million related to deconsolidation and write-down of a joint venture, and an investment valuation loss. Unplanned downtime at Decatur East was also a negative impact. Animal Nutrition results of $10 million were 91% lower compared to the prior year primarily driven by the normalization of amino acid margins and lower volumes.

Other and Corporate Summary

For the fourth quarter, Other segment operating profit was $146 million, up 64% compared to the prior year period. 

For the full year, Other segment operating profit was $375 million, up 125% compared to the prior year. Higher Captive Insurance results on new program premiums were partially offset by higher claim losses. ADM Investor Services results improved on higher net interest income. 

In Corporate, for the full year, net interest expense increased year-over-year on higher short term interest rates. Unallocated corporate costs increased versus the prior year on higher global technology spend to support digital transformation efforts. Other Corporate was unfavorable compared to the prior year due to one-time investment valuation losses of approximately $57 million. 

Outlook

The Company provided guidance for the full year 2024. ADM expects adjusted earnings per share in the range of $5.25 to $6.25 per share^{2}, down 18% at the midpoint compared to 2023, reflecting moderating margin conditions and higher costs offsetting improved volumes. 

In AS&O, global grain and oilseed supply is expected to increase as anticipated improvements in weather would support larger production levels in key South American countries. Assuming commodity prices ease from recent highs and trade flows adjust to the dislocations created over the past two years, the Company anticipates global soybean crush margin will decline in 2024, likely moving into a range of $35/Metric Ton (MT) to $60/MT. From the demand side, we continue to expect vegetable oil demand growth from renewable diesel and low single digit soybean meal demand growth to support structural margin improvement. 

In Carbohydrate Solutions, we anticipate strong volumes and lower energy costs to support margin expansion in starches and sweeteners, partially offset by lower milling margins and ethanol margins, leading to slightly lower operating income versus 2023. 

In Nutrition, we expect mid single digit revenue growth and operating income to be higher versus 2023. 

Share Repurchase Authorization

ADM also announced the Company’s Board has authorized management to repurchase an additional $2 billion of the Company’s shares under ADM’s existing 200 million share repurchase program that runs through 2024. The Company intends to initiate this capital return expeditiously utilizing available cash on hand and intends to make approximately $1 billion of this capital return through an accelerated share repurchase (“ASR”). 

As of December 31, 2023, ADM had approximately 52 million shares remaining for repurchase under its existing 200 million share program which commenced in 2015 and was then increased and extended in 2019. Since 2015, ADM has repurchased $8.6 billion of its common stock under this program. 

^{2} Forecasted GAAP Earnings Reconciliation: ADM is not presenting forecasted GAAP earnings per diluted share or a quantitative reconciliation to forecasted adjusted earnings per diluted share in reliance on the unreasonable efforts exemption provided under Item 10(e)(1)(i)(B) of Regulation S-K. The Company provided guidance for the full year 2024. ADM expects adjusted earnings per share in the range of $5.25 to $6.25 per share^{2}, down 18% at the midpoint compared to 2023, reflecting moderating margin conditions and higher costs offsetting improved volumes. 

In AS&O, global grain and oilseed supply is expected to increase as anticipated improvements in weather would support larger production levels in key South American countries. Assuming commodity prices ease from recent highs and trade flows adjust to the dislocations created over the past two years, the Company anticipates global soybean crush margin will decline in 2024, likely moving into a range of $35/Metric Ton (MT) to $60/MT. From the demand side, we continue to expect vegetable oil demand growth from renewable diesel and low single digit soybean meal demand growth to support structural margin improvement. 

In Carbohydrate Solutions, we anticipate strong volumes and lower energy costs to support margin expansion in starches and sweeteners, partially offset by lower milling margins and ethanol margins, leading to slightly lower operating income versus 2023. 

In Nutrition, we expect mid single digit revenue growth and operating income to be higher versus 2023. 

Share Repurchase Authorization

ADM also announced the Company’s Board has authorized management to repurchase an additional $2 billion of the Company’s shares under ADM’s existing 200 million share repurchase program that runs through 2024. The Company intends to initiate this capital return expeditiously utilizing available cash on hand and intends to make approximately $1 billion of this capital return through an accelerated share repurchase (“ASR”). 

As of December 31, 2023, ADM had approximately 52 million shares remaining for repurchase under its existing 200 million share program which commenced in 2015 and was then increased and extended in 2019. Since 2015, ADM has repurchased $8.6 billion of its common stock under this program.

#### Executive Summary
**Company Name**: Deep Water Fossils  
**Location**: Wilmington, NC  
**Brand**: Deep Water Fossils  
**Logo**: [Insert Logo]  
**Mission Statement**: To provide high-quality, authentic fossilized shark teeth to collectors, enthusiasts, and retailers worldwide.

**Objectives**:
- Establish Deep Water Fossils as a leading provider of fossilized shark teeth.
- Increase sales through a combination of retail and wholesale channels.
- Build a loyal customer base through exceptional product quality and customer service.

#### Business Description
**Overview**: Deep Water Fossils specializes in sourcing and selling fossilized shark teeth, primarily focusing on Megalodon teeth. Utilizing a 46-foot boat equipped for extended trips, the company leverages known dive locations off the coast of North Carolina to find high-quality fossils. Sales are conducted through an established Etsy shop and supported by active social media marketing on Facebook and Instagram.

**Resources**:
1. 46-foot boat capable of 2-3 day trips.
2. Complete dive equipment.
3. Access to known productive dive locations.
4. Retail shop on Etsy.
5. Established brand and logo.
6. Social media presence on Facebook and Instagram.

#### Market Analysis
**Industry Overview**: The fossil collectibles market is robust, with high demand for authentic, well-preserved shark teeth, particularly Megalodon teeth.

**Target Market**:
- **Collectors**: Individuals seeking unique and rare fossil specimens.
- **Retailers**: Shops and souvenir stores looking for bulk purchases.
- **Institutions**: Museums and educational organizations interested in display and study specimens.

**Competitive Analysis**:
- **Strengths**: High-quality, self-sourced products; established online presence; strong brand identity.
- **Weaknesses**: Limited wholesale connections; reliance on seasonal diving conditions.
- **Opportunities**: Expansion into wholesale markets; increased participation in fossil shows.
- **Threats**: Market competition; potential regulatory changes.

#### Marketing Strategy
**Branding**: 
- Consistent use of the Deep Water Fossils brand and logo across all marketing materials.
- Emphasis on authenticity, quality, and the adventure of fossil hunting.

**Sales Channels**:
- **Online**: Primary sales through the Etsy shop. Utilize SEO and targeted ads to drive traffic.
- **Wholesale**: Develop relationships with retail shops, museums, and educational institutions.
- **Physical Events**: Participate in fossil shows and trade fairs to increase visibility and direct sales.

**Marketing Tactics**:
- **Social Media**: Regular posts on Facebook and Instagram featuring dive trips, new finds, and customer testimonials. Use paid ads to boost visibility.
- **Content Marketing**: Create engaging content, such as blog posts and videos, showcasing the fossil hunting process and educational information about shark teeth.
- **Email Marketing**: Build an email list through the Etsy shop and social media. Send regular newsletters with updates, special offers, and educational content.

#### Operations Plan
**Diving Operations**:
- Schedule regular 2-3 day diving trips using the 46-foot boat to known locations.
- Implement safety protocols and ensure all equipment is maintained and ready for use.

**Inventory Management**:
- Sort and categorize teeth by size and quality upon return from each trip.
- Photograph and list items on Etsy with detailed descriptions and prices.

**Customer Service**:
- Ensure prompt responses to customer inquiries.
- Offer free gifts with purchases and a satisfaction guarantee to build customer loyalty.

- **Background**: Fossilized shark teeth, particularly those of the Megalodon, are highly sought after by collectors and enthusiasts.

- **Methodology**: Data was collected through online marketplace analysis, industry reports, and surveys/interviews with the fossil enthusiast community.

# Biden-Harris Administration Makes Historic, $11 Billion Investment to Advance Clean Energy Across Rural America Through Investing in America Agenda

Two new programs made possible by the Inflation Reduction Act will support clean and affordable energy, new jobs and healthier communities

### Release & Contact Info

Press Release

Release No. 0111.23

Contact: USDA Press  
Email: press@usda.gov

WASHINGTON, May 16, 2023 – The Biden-Harris Administration today announced the availability of nearly $11 billion in grants and loan opportunities that will help rural energy and utility providers bring affordable, reliable clean energy to their communities across the country. This represents the single largest investment in rural electrification since President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Rural Electrification Act into law in 1936.

“The Biden-Harris Administration’s commitment to cleaner energy provides rural communities with an affordable and reliable power grid, while supporting thousands of new jobs and helping lower energy costs in the future,” Agriculture Secretary Tom Vilsack said. “These investments will also combat climate change and significantly reduce air and water pollution that put children’s health at risk. The U.S. Department of Agriculture stands ready to partner with municipalities, tribal entities, entrepreneurs, rural electric cooperatives and other utilities to see this transformative investment come to life and create new economic growth and healthier communities.”

Funding is available through two programs under President Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act, which makes the nation’s largest-ever investment in combatting the climate crisis. Specifically, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will be opening a Letter of Interest process for the Empowering Rural America (“New ERA”) program, which makes $9.7 billion available to eligible rural electric cooperatives to deploy renewable energy systems, zero-emission and carbon capture systems. In addition to New ERA, USDA will also be opening a Letter of Interest process for the Powering Affordable Clean Energy (PACE) program, which makes $1 billion available in partially forgivable loans to renewable-energy developers and electric service providers, including municipals, cooperatives, and investor-owned and Tribal utilities to help finance large-scale solar, wind, geothermal, biomass, hydropower projects and energy storage in support of renewable energy systems.

“This new funding from the Inflation Reduction Act shows that President Biden, and our entire administration, is serious about investing in rural America,” said John Podesta, Senior Advisor to the President for Clean Energy Innovation and Implementation. “This announcement embodies what the Investing in America Agenda is all about—building a clean energy economy that works for everyone.”

Together, these two programs represent the single largest investment in rural electrification since President Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Rural Electrification Act into law in 1936. This announcement is part of President Biden’s Investing in America agenda to grow the American economy from the bottom up and the middle out by rebuilding our nation’s infrastructure, driving more than $435 billion in private-sector manufacturing investments, creating good-paying jobs, and building a clean-energy economy to tackle the climate crisis and make our communities more resilient.

“All across America, rural cooperatives lift up our rural communities. President Biden’s investment agenda positions his Agriculture Department as the ultimate partner in this work – financing not just upgrades to clean and affordable power, but also economic empowerment and uplift,” said Ali Zaidi, Assistant to the President and National Climate Advisor. “For so many of our rural communities, this is simply a gamechanger. It’s a big deal.”

More information on the New ERA program is available at 【49†www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/electric-programs/empowering-rural-america-new-era-program†www.rd.usda.gov】. Rural electric cooperatives, including current and previous USDA borrowers, are eligible for funding. To apply, eligible entities must submit a Letter of Interest between July 31 and Aug. 31, 2023.

More information on the PACE program is available at 【50†www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/electric-programs/powering-affordable-clean-energy-pace-program†www.rd.usda.gov】. Loans through this program may be forgiven by 40% of the loan amount, and the maximum loan amount is $100 million. Applicants in Puerto Rico, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Republic of Palau, and Tribal communities are eligible for up to 60% loan forgiveness. For this program, USDA will begin accepting Letters of Interest starting on June 30, 2023, on a rolling basis until Sept. 29, 2023.

The goal of the PACE program is to make clean energy affordable for vulnerable, disadvantaged, Tribal and energy communities to heat their homes, run their businesses and power their cars, schools, hospitals and more. USDA may be able to leverage nearly $3 billion in projects through this program. This is in line with President Biden’s 【51†Justice40 Initiative†www.whitehouse.gov】, which aims to ensure that 40% of the overall benefits of certain federal investments reach disadvantaged communities that are marginalized and overburdened by pollution.

Background: Inflation Reduction Act

The Biden-Harris Administration championed the Inflation Reduction Act to help provide new funding and unprecedented incentives to expand clean energy, transform rural power production, create jobs and spur economic growth.

The Inflation Reduction Act provides several funding opportunities to USDA Rural Development to help eligible organizations invest in renewable energy infrastructure and zero-emission systems and make energy-efficiency improvements that will significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

For example, the Inflation Reduction Act provides up to $2 billion for the 【52†Rural Energy for America Program†www.rd.usda.gov】 (REAP), with $303 million set aside for underutilized technologies and technical assistance. USDA anticipates funds will support renewable energy and energy-efficiency projects for more than 41,500 farms and small businesses.

The Inflation Reduction Act also provides up to $500 million in grants for 【53†infrastructure improvements to blend, store or distribute biofuels†www.rd.usda.gov】 to give consumers more fueling options. This includes installing, retrofitting or upgrading dispensers for ethanol at retail fueling stations, as well as home heating oil distribution centers.

For more information on the Inflation Reduction Act, visit: 【54†www.rd.usda.gov/inflation-reduction-act†www.rd.usda.gov】.

USDA touches the lives of all Americans each day in so many positive ways. Under the Biden-Harris Administration, USDA is transforming America’s food system with a greater focus on more resilient local and regional food production, fairer markets for all producers, ensuring access to safe, healthy and nutritious food in all communities, building new markets and streams of income for farmers and producers using climate-smart food and forestry practices, making historic investments in infrastructure and clean energy capabilities in rural America, and committing to equity across the Department by removing systemic barriers and building a workforce more representative of America. To learn more, visit 【1†www.usda.gov】.

Now, let's focus on the Objectives and Goals.

**Question for Objectives and Goals**: What are the specific targets and expected outcomes of your green methanol plant project? This could include production capacity, environmental goals like CO2 reduction, or other measurable impacts you aim to achieve.

**Project Feasibility and Sustainability of the Green Methanol Plant Using Forest Harvest Residuals**

The feasibility and sustainability of the Eco-Synergy project are grounded in several key aspects:

1. **Technical Feasibility**:
   - **Advanced Gasification Technology**: The project leverages state-of-the-art gasification technology, which has been proven effective in converting biomass into syngas.
   - **Scalable Design**: The plant's design is scalable, allowing for adjustments based on the availability of feedstock and market demand.

2. **Economic Feasibility**:
   - **Market Analysis**: The growing demand for sustainable fuels, especially in the maritime industry, presents a viable market for green methanol.
   - **Cost-Benefit Analysis**: Initial investments are offset by the long-term economic benefits from the sale of methanol and the potential to capitalize on carbon credits.

3. **Logistical Feasibility**:
   - **Supply Chain Management**: Reliable sourcing of forest harvest residuals is ensured through partnerships with local forest managers and landowners.
   - **Transportation and Storage**: Efficient logistics are in place for the transportation and storage of both the feedstock and the finished product.

4. **Environmental Sustainability**:
   - **Renewable Feedstock**: Using forest residuals aligns with principles of sustainability, as it repurposes waste materials without depleting natural resources.
   - **Emissions Reduction**: The production process is designed to minimize emissions, and the end product contributes to the reduction of greenhouse gases.

5. **Social Sustainability**:
   - **Community Engagement**: The project includes plans for engaging with local communities, ensuring transparency and addressing any concerns.
   - **Educational Outreach**: Opportunities for local educational initiatives are incorporated, fostering awareness and support for renewable energy.

6. **Regulatory Compliance**:
   - The project adheres to all relevant environmental and industrial regulations and standards, ensuring legal and ethical compliance.

7. **Long-Term Viability**:
   - **Continuous Improvement**: The plant will adapt to advancements in technology and changes in market dynamics to maintain its relevance and effectiveness.

This comprehensive approach ensures that the Eco-Synergy project is not only feasible from multiple perspectives but also sustains its viability and relevance in the long term.

---

Would you like to further discuss any specific elements of the project's feasibility and sustainability, or shall we move on to the next section, which is Team and Expertise?

**Technology and Methodology for the Green Methanol Plant Using Forest Harvest Residuals**

**Collection and Preparation of Biomass**:
The project starts with the gathering of forest harvest residuals such as branches, bark, and leaves. These materials are then chipped or ground to ensure consistency in size and texture, preparing them for the gasification process.

**Gasification**:
In this crucial step, the prepared biomass is heated in a low-oxygen environment. This process transforms the biomass into syngas, a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, and some carbon dioxide. Advanced reactors, like fluidized bed gasifiers, are employed for their efficiency and effectiveness in this transformation.

**Syngas Cleaning and Conditioning**:
The produced syngas contains impurities and varying gas ratios. To ensure it's suitable for methanol production, the syngas undergoes a cleaning process to remove contaminants like tar. It's then conditioned to adjust the carbon monoxide to hydrogen ratio, which is crucial for the subsequent methanol synthesis.

**Methanol Synthesis**:
The clean, conditioned syngas is then passed over a catalyst, commonly copper-based, under high pressure and temperature. This catalytic process triggers a chemical reaction that converts the syngas into methanol.

**Distillation**:
Finally, the produced methanol is purified through distillation to meet the required quality standards, ensuring it's suitable for use as a fuel.

**Innovative Aspects**:
- **Integrated Systems**: The plant may incorporate systems that integrate biomass gasification with energy recovery, improving overall efficiency and reducing waste.
- **Catalyst Development**: Ongoing advances in catalyst technology enhance the efficiency of the methanol synthesis process, potentially leading to higher yields and lower costs.
- **Carbon Capture and Utilization**: Incorporating carbon capture techniques into the process can further reduce the overall carbon footprint of the methanol production, aligning with global carbon neutrality goals.

This detailed description of the technology and methodology demonstrates the project's commitment to innovation and efficiency, highlighting its potential as a sustainable energy solution.

---

Shall we proceed to the Environmental Impact section, or is there any aspect of the Technology and Methodology you'd like to delve into further?

**Environmental Impact of the Green Methanol Plant Using Forest Harvest Residuals**

The Eco-Synergy project is designed with a strong emphasis on positive environmental impact, addressing several key areas:

1. **Reduction in Forest Waste and Fire Risk**:
   - By utilizing forest harvest residuals as feedstock, the project significantly reduces waste left in forests. This not only clears potential fuel for forest fires, thereby mitigating fire risks, but also contributes to healthier forest ecosystems.

2. **Lower Carbon Footprint**:
   - The process of converting forest residuals into methanol results in a fuel that, when burned, emits significantly less CO2 compared to traditional fossil fuels. This directly contributes to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, a crucial factor in combatting climate change.

3. **Sustainable Resource Use**:
   - Using forest residuals, a renewable resource, for fuel production represents a sustainable approach to resource utilization. It transforms what is typically considered waste into a valuable energy source, promoting a circular economy.

4. **Contribution to Biodiversity**:
   - Efficiently managing forest waste can lead to healthier forests, which supports biodiversity. Healthier forests are more resilient and provide better habitats for wildlife.

5. **Potential for Carbon Capture and Storage**:
   - Integrating carbon capture technologies in the production process could further reduce the plant's carbon footprint, making the produced methanol even more environmentally friendly.

6. **Improving Air Quality**:
   - Green methanol as an alternative fuel can lead to improved air quality, particularly in maritime applications, by replacing dirtier fuels that release higher levels of pollutants.

7. **Alignment with Climate Goals**:
   - The project aligns with global and national climate goals by providing a practical solution to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and promoting cleaner energy sources.

This comprehensive approach to environmental impact demonstrates the project's commitment to sustainability and its potential as a model for future green energy initiatives.

---

Are you ready to proceed to the Economic Impact section, or is there an aspect of the Environmental Impact you'd like to explore more?

**Eco-Synergy: Green Methanol Production from Forest Harvest Residuals**

**Project Overview**:
Eco-Synergy is a groundbreaking project that transforms forest harvest residuals into green methanol, leveraging advanced gasification technology. This initiative represents a sustainable approach to energy production, diverging from traditional fossil-fuel-based methods. By utilizing a renewable and often overlooked resource, Eco-Synergy addresses waste reduction and contributes to carbon footprint minimization, making a significant impact in renewable energy solutions.

**Problem Statement**:
The maritime industry currently faces the challenge of reducing its carbon footprint while maintaining operational efficiency. Eco-Synergy provides a solution by producing carbon-neutral green methanol, compatible with existing maritime engines and fuel systems, thus offering an environmentally friendly alternative to traditional maritime fuels.

**Objectives and Goals**:
1. Environmental Management: Provide a market for forest residuals, reducing waste and forest fire risks.
2. Economic Benefit: Enhance forest value and management options for landowners.
3. Production Capacity: Process 2 million green tons of feedstock annually to produce 500,000 tons of methanol.
4. Carbon Emission Reduction: Achieve lower net carbon emissions compared to heavy oil fuels.

**Technology and Methodology**:
Eco-Synergy employs a multi-step process, starting with the collection and preparation of biomass, followed by efficient gasification to produce syngas. This syngas is then cleaned and conditioned before being converted into methanol through a catalytic process. Innovative aspects include integrated systems for efficiency, advances in catalyst technology, and potential carbon capture.

**Environmental Impact**:
The project significantly contributes to environmental sustainability by reducing forest waste and associated fire risks, lowering carbon emissions, promoting renewable resource use, and potentially integrating carbon capture technologies.

**Economic Impact**:
Eco-Synergy stimulates local employment, generates revenue for forest owners, boosts the local economy, diversifies the energy sector, and promotes global market potential for green methanol.

**Project Feasibility and Sustainability**:
With a focus on technical, economic, and logistical feasibility, Eco-Synergy demonstrates its commitment to long-term viability. The project employs proven technologies, ensures supply chain reliability, and adheres to environmental and industrial regulations.

**Team and Expertise**:
The project is backed by a skilled team including experienced managers, renewable energy engineers, environmental scientists, market strategists, financial experts, logistics managers, community engagement professionals, and legal and regulatory experts.

**Budget and Funding Requirements**:
Estimated at $2 billion, the project has secured equity and plans to finance the majority through debt. Additional funding assistance is sought to bridge the gap to full operationalization (TRL 9).

**Conclusion and Call to Action**:
Eco-Synergy invites government bodies and stakeholders to join in this sustainable venture. Your support is pivotal in achieving our shared goal of environmental innovation and economic growth.

This cohesive document encapsulates the essence of the Eco-Synergy project, highlighting its innovative, environmental, and economic aspects, and inviting collaboration for a sustainable future.

The toroidal design tends to make a propeller more stiff compared to traditional designs. This increased stiffness can be attributed to the structural characteristics of the toroidal shape itself. 

1. **Looped Blade Structure**: The toroidal propeller typically has a looped blade design, where the tip of one blade curves back into its trailing edge. This closed-form design inherently provides more structural stability and stiffness compared to open-bladed designs.

2. **Distributed Stress**: In a toroidal propeller, the stresses induced during operation are more evenly distributed across the blade structure. This distribution of forces contributes to the overall stiffness of the propeller, reducing the likelihood of blade deformation under load.

3. **Material Usage**: The manufacturing of toroidal propellers often involves advanced materials and techniques, which can further enhance the stiffness and durability of the propeller.

4. **Vortex Minimization**: The toroidal design minimizes the strength of trailing tip vortices, which are typically a source of stress and potential deformation in traditional propeller blades. By reducing these vortices, the propeller experiences less dynamic stress, contributing to its stiffness.

In summary, the structural characteristics of the toroidal propeller, including its looped blade design and even stress distribution, contribute to its increased stiffness. This can be advantageous in reducing vibration and enhancing the durability of the propeller.

Several shipbuilding and marine propeller manufacturers have conducted studies and trials on toroidal propellers, particularly for larger vessels. One notable company in this field is Sharrow Engineering, known for their Sharrow Propeller MX-1. This toroidal boat propeller has shown impressive results in extensive sea trials, exhibiting efficiency gains of between 9-15% over comparable 3-blade propeller designs. The MX-1's design includes 'tipless' loops for each blade, reducing tip vortices that can cause noise and vibration. Sharrow Engineering has also explored applications of toroidal propellers for larger vessels, such as 65ft planing motoryachts and even simulated tests for super tankers, showing similar theoretical efficiency gains【23†source】.

In addition to Sharrow Engineering, there are several leading global ship propeller manufacturers that focus on innovation and high performance in propeller design, although specific studies on toroidal propellers by these companies weren't found. These manufacturers include VEEM Propellers, Teignbridge Propellers International Ltd, Stone Marine Propulsion, and Mecklenburger Metallguss GmbH. They specialize in bespoke designs and are known for their technological advances in propeller manufacturing【22†source】.

Furthermore, the benefits of toroidal propellers, as explored by various sources, include increased efficiency, maneuverability, noise reduction, reduced cavitation, better fuel economy, lower vibrations, compact design, and adaptability for various types of vessels, including commercial ships, yachts, and submarines【24†source】【25†source】.

These developments suggest a growing interest and application of toroidal propellers in the marine industry, extending from small boats to large commercial vessels. The innovation in this field focuses on enhancing efficiency, reducing environmental impact, and improving vessel performance.

#  Sharrow MX-1: This toroidal boat propeller could be top of the props 

【42† Hugo Andreae 】  May 28, 2020 

  [Image 1: sharrow-mx-1-toroidal boat propeller] 

Hugo Andreae takes a look at a revolutionary new toroidal boat propeller said to be faster and more efficient than rivals 

A radical new toroidal boat propeller is being touted as the single biggest advance in propeller design since the 1930s. Claimed to deliver significant fuel savings across all different types and sizes of craft as well as faster planing, higher top speeds, superior handling and reduced vibration, it sounds almost too good to be true.

However, extensive sea trials carried out by US website 【43†boattest.com†boattest.com】 on the new Sharrow Propeller MX-1 seem to confirm all of the above and show efficiency gains of between 9-15% over comparable 3-blade propeller designs.

The tests were carried out on a 20ft Bayliner VR5 【8†sportsboat】 fitted with a standard Mercury 150hp 【44†outboard】 engine, comparing Sharrow’s new tipless MX-1 against two market leading 【45†boat propellers†www.pbo.co.uk】.

Not only was it the fastest of the three (41.7 knots vs 40.8 knots and 39.0 knots) and the most efficient (4.6mpg @ 32 knots vs 4.2mpg and 4.1mph), it also planed earlier and outperformed them both at every 500rpm increment from idle speed to wide open throttle.

[Image 2: sharrow-mx-1-propeller-close-up]

Each blade of the Sharrow MX-1 forms a single ‘tipless’ loop

### Recommended videos for you

This is crucial, as propellers that are designed to give the highest possible top speed often struggle at low to medium revs, and vice versa. So how is Sharrow Engineering claiming to have cracked the conundrum that has stymied so many others?

### Tip troubles

As ever it seems to be a combination of inspiration and perspiration. The inspiration came from its inventor and CEO of Sharrow Engineering, Greg Sharrow, a music graduate, who originally set out to solve a very different problem.

He wanted to use 【46†camera drones†www.yachtingworld.com】 to film performers in action but soon found that their microphones would pick up the noise of the drones. He realised that most of this noise was not being created by the drone’s tiny electric motors but by the propeller tip vortices.

[Image 3: Propeller-tip-vortices-credit-Rachel-Sloman-flickr]

Visible tip vortices on an aeroplane propeller. Photo: Rachel Sloman / Flickr

These swirling pockets of turbulence are caused by high-pressure air on one side of the blade rushing round to meet the low pressure air on the other, creating induced drag, noise and vibration. The same principle applies to boat propellers, where the tip vortices are even more pronounced and can lead to cavitation, when water is momentarily vapourised by the sudden change in pressure creating bubbles.

Greg reasoned that if he could reduce or even eliminate these tip vortices, it should lead to a quieter, more efficient drone. His light bulb moment came on a dog walk when the idea of a tipless blade, that loops round to rejoin the propeller hub like a strip of twisted ribbon, first popped into his head.

It took a further seven years of intensive research and development, substantial investment, 23 worldwide patents and a switch in focus from drones to boats before Sharrow Engineering unveiled its first production toroidal boat propeller at the 【25†Miami Boat Show】 in February.

Since then it has already won an award for innovation and the company says it is now in discussion with a number of major propeller and engine manufacturers.

【42† Hugo Andreae 】  May 28, 2020

Hugo Andreae takes a look at a revolutionary new toroidal boat propeller said to be faster and more efficient than rivals 

A radical new toroidal boat propeller is being touted as the single biggest advance in propeller design since the 1930s. Claimed to deliver significant fuel savings across all different types and sizes of craft as well as faster planing, higher top speeds, superior handling and reduced vibration, it sounds almost too good to be true.

However, extensive sea trials carried out by US website 【43†boattest.com†boattest.com】 on the new Sharrow Propeller MX-1 seem to confirm all of the above and show efficiency gains of between 9-15% over comparable 3-blade propeller designs.

The tests were carried out on a 20ft Bayliner VR5 【8†sportsboat】 fitted with a standard Mercury 150hp 【44†outboard】 engine, comparing Sharrow’s new tipless MX-1 against two market leading 【45†boat propellers†www.pbo.co.uk】.

Not only was it the fastest of the three (41.7 knots vs 40.8 knots and 39.0 knots) and the most efficient (4.6mpg @ 32 knots vs 4.2mpg and 4.1mph), it also planed earlier and outperformed them both at every 500rpm increment from idle speed to wide open throttle.

[Image 2: sharrow-mx-1-propeller-close-up]

Each blade of the Sharrow MX-1 forms a single ‘tipless’ loop

This is crucial, as propellers that are designed to give the highest possible top speed often struggle at low to medium revs, and vice versa. So how is Sharrow Engineering claiming to have cracked the conundrum that has stymied so many others?

### Tip troubles

As ever it seems to be a combination of inspiration and perspiration. The inspiration came from its inventor and CEO of Sharrow Engineering, Greg Sharrow, a music graduate, who originally set out to solve a very different problem.

He wanted to use 【46†camera drones†www.yachtingworld.com】 to film performers in action but soon found that their microphones would pick up the noise of the drones. He realised that most of this noise was not being created by the drone’s tiny electric motors but by the propeller tip vortices.

[Image 3: Propeller-tip-vortices-credit-Rachel-Sloman-flickr]

Visible tip vortices on an aeroplane propeller. Photo: Rachel Sloman / Flickr

These swirling pockets of turbulence are caused by high-pressure air on one side of the blade rushing round to meet the low pressure air on the other, creating induced drag, noise and vibration. The same principle applies to boat propellers, where the tip vortices are even more pronounced and can lead to cavitation, when water is momentarily vapourised by the sudden change in pressure creating bubbles.

Greg reasoned that if he could reduce or even eliminate these tip vortices, it should lead to a quieter, more efficient drone. His light bulb moment came on a dog walk when the idea of a tipless blade, that loops round to rejoin the propeller hub like a strip of twisted ribbon, first popped into his head.

It took a further seven years of intensive research and development, substantial investment, 23 worldwide patents and a switch in focus from drones to boats before Sharrow Engineering unveiled its first production toroidal boat propeller at the 【25†Miami Boat Show】 in February.

Since then it has already won an award for innovation and the company says it is now in discussion with a number of major propeller and engine manufacturers.

2. **University of Michigan’s Marine Hydrodynamics Laboratory**: They have been involved in modeling and prototype work for toroidal boat propellers, conducting scale tank testing to prove their findings. This includes tests on large-scale applications, such as displacement trawler yachts, container ships, and super tankers【14†source】.

3. **MITRE**: Also collaborated with MIT on the development of the toroidal propeller. Their involvement indicates a broader range of application and interest from various sectors【11†source】.

4. **NASA**: Their research has highlighted the human perception of drone noise, which has been a driving factor in the development of quieter propellers like the toroidal propeller by MIT. This collaboration suggests an interest in applying these findings in aerospace technologies【11†source】.

These institutions and collaborations show a diverse interest in the development and application of toroidal propellers, from small drones to large maritime vessels. The combined efforts of these researchers are pushing the boundaries of propeller efficiency and noise reduction.

Lincoln Laboratory shares this award with its collaborators on the technology: the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration, MITRE, and Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory.

Constrained Communications and Radar Dual-Use  

Radar and wireless communications systems typically operate in separate radio frequency (RF) bands to avoid cross-interference. However, today’s abundance of wireless devices is crowding the RF spectrum — a problem that is leading researchers to explore ways for technologies to share the same RF bands to free up space.  

The Constrained Communications and Radar Dual-Use (CONCORD) technology enables such band sharing. CONCORD is a method of designing waveforms that can perform both radar and communications tasks simultaneously, with the same transmitter and receiver. This method allows a system designer to unify the hardware used for these tasks, simplifying a system's design and lowering costs. CONCORD has applications for any military or commercial systems that need to sense objects with radar and send out data, such as airborne radar imaging systems or self-driving cars. 

Embedded microjet cooling for high-power electronics  

Electronics are becoming smaller and more powerful. These increased power densities are approaching the limit of what conventional thermal architectures can manage. Electronics designers are thus looking for new cooling solutions to meet performance requirements and reduce energy costs.  

Lincoln Laboratory's embedded microjet cooling technology uses arrays of micron-scale fluid jets to cool high-power devices. These arrays are small enough to be embedded directly into the device at the chip level. This integration allows fluid to flow directly up to the electronics' semiconductor substrate, delivering an order-of-magnitude improvement in heat transfer over heat sinks or cold plates that pass cooling fluid parallel to the substrate. The microjets can be fabricated from low-cost materials, such as silicon or plastics, and can be mass produced with existing foundry tools. An MIT spinoff company, JETCOOL Technologies Inc., is commercializing this technology.

Toroidal propeller  

Anyone who has encountered a small hobby drone flying nearby has likely noticed the high-pitched buzz of its propellers. 【41†Experiments by NASA†ntrs.nasa.gov】 have shown that humans find this sound to be more annoying than any other vehicle noise. If drones are to be accepted for wider use, such as for package delivery, they’ll likely need to be quieter.  

Lincoln Laboratory's toroidal propeller is significantly quieter than common multirotor propellers, while producing comparable thrust. The toroidal propeller consists of looped blades, in which the tip of a leading propeller blade is curved back into its trailing propeller blade. This closed structure minimizes the strength of trailing tip vortices and increases the overall stiffness of the propeller, both of which reduce its noise; it is also less likely than conventional propellers to catch on or cut objects in its path. The propeller can be 3D printed and customized to a range of vehicles, making it suitable as a drop-in replacement on current drones.

Timely Address Space Randomization  

Timely Address Space Randomization (TASR) addresses the problem of memory corruption, one of today's most prevalent cyber vulnerabilities. Hackers who launch memory corruption attacks can gain control of or steal data from millions of computers at once because the memory structures in these systems all look alike. TASR prevents such attacks by automatically shuffling, or re-randomizing, the location of code in memory.  

TASR improves upon an existing solution deployed in most modern operating systems, called address space layout randomization (ASLR), which uses a similar premise of randomizing memory layout. The problem with ASLR is that it randomizes memory just once, and attackers have worked around that solution by using "information-leakage attacks" to force an application to reveal how its memory has been randomized. TASR is the first technology to mitigate such attacks by randomizing layout every time it observes an output from an application. TASR is compatible with existing cyber infrastructure and incurs a very low overhead. InfoSiftr, a cloud development company, has licensed TASR.

TROPICS Pathfinder satellite  

According to the 【42†National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration†www.gfdl.noaa.gov】, the frequency and intensity of hurricanes are expected to rise throughout this century. To provide scientists with more data over the Earth's tropical belt where these storms form, Lincoln Laboratory conceived of the 【43†TROPICS†tropics.ll.mit.edu】 mission. TROPICS is a constellation of small satellites, called CubeSats, that will work together to provide global, rapid-revisit views of tropical storms. The 【44†TROPICS Pathfinder satellite†www.ll.mit.edu】【45† 】was launched in 2021 as the first in this constellation.  

Aboard the satellite is a microwave sounder, a sensor that produces high-resolution, 3D images of the temperature and water vapor content of

However, extensive sea trials carried out by US website 【43†boattest.com†boattest.com】 on the new Sharrow Propeller MX-1 seem to confirm all of the above and show efficiency gains of between 9-15% over comparable 3-blade propeller designs.

The tests were carried out on a 20ft Bayliner VR5 【8†sportsboat】 fitted with a standard Mercury 150hp 【44†outboard】 engine, comparing Sharrow’s new tipless MX-1 against two market leading 【45†boat propellers†www.pbo.co.uk】.

Not only was it the fastest of the three (41.7 knots vs 40.8 knots and 39.0 knots) and the most efficient (4.6mpg @ 32 knots vs 4.2mpg and 4.1mph), it also planed earlier and outperformed them both at every 500rpm increment from idle speed to wide open throttle.

[Image 2: sharrow-mx-1-propeller-close-up]

Each blade of the Sharrow MX-1 forms a single ‘tipless’ loop

### Recommended videos for you

This is crucial, as propellers that are designed to give the highest possible top speed often struggle at low to medium revs, and vice versa. So how is Sharrow Engineering claiming to have cracked the conundrum that has stymied so many others?

### Tip troubles

As ever it seems to be a combination of inspiration and perspiration. The inspiration came from its inventor and CEO of Sharrow Engineering, Greg Sharrow, a music graduate, who originally set out to solve a very different problem.

He wanted to use 【46†camera drones†www.yachtingworld.com】 to film performers in action but soon found that their microphones would pick up the noise of the drones. He realised that most of this noise was not being created by the drone’s tiny electric motors but by the propeller tip vortices.

[Image 3: Propeller-tip-vortices-credit-Rachel-Sloman-flickr]

Visible tip vortices on an aeroplane propeller. Photo: Rachel Sloman / Flickr

These swirling pockets of turbulence are caused by high-pressure air on one side of the blade rushing round to meet the low pressure air on the other, creating induced drag, noise and vibration. The same principle applies to boat propellers, where the tip vortices are even more pronounced and can lead to cavitation, when water is momentarily vapourised by the sudden change in pressure creating bubbles.

Greg reasoned that if he could reduce or even eliminate these tip vortices, it should lead to a quieter, more efficient drone. His light bulb moment came on a dog walk when the idea of a tipless blade, that loops round to rejoin the propeller hub like a strip of twisted ribbon, first popped into his head.

It took a further seven years of intensive research and development, substantial investment, 23 worldwide patents and a switch in focus from drones to boats before Sharrow Engineering unveiled its first production toroidal boat propeller at the 【25†Miami Boat Show】 in February.

Since then it has already won an award for innovation and the company says it is now in discussion with a number of major propeller and engine manufacturers.

However, extensive sea trials carried out by US website 【43†boattest.com†boattest.com】 on the new Sharrow Propeller MX-1 seem to confirm all of the above and show efficiency gains of between 9-15% over comparable 3-blade propeller designs.

The tests were carried out on a 20ft Bayliner VR5 【8†sportsboat】 fitted with a standard Mercury 150hp 【44†outboard】 engine, comparing Sharrow’s new tipless MX-1 against two market leading 【45†boat propellers†www.pbo.co.uk】.

Not only was it the fastest of the three (41.7 knots vs 40.8 knots and 39.0 knots) and the most efficient (4.6mpg @ 32 knots vs 4.2mpg and 4.1mph), it also planed earlier and outperformed them both at every 500rpm increment from idle speed to wide open throttle.

[Image 2: sharrow-mx-1-propeller-close-up]

Each blade of the Sharrow MX-1 forms a single ‘tipless’ loop

### Recommended videos for you

This is crucial, as propellers that are designed to give the highest possible top speed often struggle at low to medium revs, and vice versa. So how is Sharrow Engineering claiming to have cracked the conundrum that has stymied so many others?

### Tip troubles

As ever it seems to be a combination of inspiration and perspiration. The inspiration came from its inventor and CEO of Sharrow Engineering, Greg Sharrow, a music graduate, who originally set out to solve a very different problem.

He wanted to use 【46†camera drones†www.yachtingworld.com】 to film performers in action but soon found that their microphones would pick up the noise of the drones. He realised that most of this noise was not being created by the drone’s tiny electric motors but by the propeller tip vortices.

[Image 3: Propeller-tip-vortices-credit-Rachel-Sloman-flickr]

Visible tip vortices on an aeroplane propeller. Photo: Rachel Sloman / Flickr

These swirling pockets of turbulence are caused by high-pressure air on one side of the blade rushing round to meet the low pressure air on the other, creating induced drag, noise and vibration. The same principle applies to boat propellers, where the tip vortices are even more pronounced and can lead to cavitation, when water is momentarily vapourised by the sudden change in pressure creating bubbles.

Greg reasoned that if he could reduce or even eliminate these tip vortices, it should lead to a quieter, more efficient drone. His light bulb moment came on a dog walk when the idea of a tipless blade, that loops round to rejoin the propeller hub like a strip of twisted ribbon, first popped into his head.

It took a further seven years of intensive research and development, substantial investment, 23 worldwide patents and a switch in focus from drones to boats before Sharrow Engineering unveiled its first production toroidal boat propeller at the 【25†Miami Boat Show】 in February.

Since then it has already won an award for innovation and the company says it is now in discussion with a number of major propeller and engine manufacturers.

In the past decade, significant advancements have been made in the field of toroidal propellers, particularly by MIT and Sharrow Engineering.

1. **MIT's Toroidal Propeller**: Developed by the MIT Lincoln Laboratory, this propeller has made strides in reducing noise levels, especially in the 1-5 kHz frequency range, which is crucial for human perception. Their unique design features looped blades, where the tip of one blade curves back into another, creating a closed form. This design effectively dissipates vortices, resulting in reduced noise. Interestingly, despite being at an early development stage, these propellers have shown to produce more thrust at a given power level compared to standard propellers. A notable aspect of this design is its potential safety benefits, as the looped shape decreases the likelihood of the propellers catching or cutting objects. However, they are complex to manufacture and may require 3D printing, potentially raising production costs【10†source】【12†source】.

2. **Sharrow Engineering's MX-1 Propeller**: This company has developed the Sharrow Propeller MX-1, which has shown efficiency gains of 9-15% over comparable 3-blade propeller designs. Extensive sea trials demonstrated that the MX-1 is faster and more efficient than its competitors. The unique aspect of the MX-1 is its ‘tipless’ looped design, which addresses issues of propeller tip vortices - swirling pockets of turbulence that create induced drag, noise, and vibration. The elimination or reduction of these vortices leads to quieter and more efficient operation. Sharrow Engineering's innovation in this field has been recognized, and the company is in discussions with major propeller and engine manufacturers for further development【14†source】.

These studies and developments highlight the ongoing evolution in propeller technology, focusing on efficiency and noise reduction. Both MIT and Sharrow Engineering are at the forefront of this innovation, demonstrating significant potential for applications in various fields, from drones to marine vehicles.

"We came up with this initial concept of using a toroidal shape, this annular wing shape, to hopefully make a quieter propeller," Sebastian continues. "I had an intern of mine, who was just absolutely phenomenal, run with the idea. He took the concept and created a bunch of iterations using 3D printers."

[Image 11: The biggest noise reductions occur right where people will want them: in the 1-5 kHz frequency range] 

The biggest noise reductions occur right where people will want them: in the 1-5 kHz frequency range 

MIT Lincoln Laboratory

Within a few attempts, the team indeed found a design that reduced not only overall noise levels at a given thrust level, but particularly noise in the 1-5 kHz range. 

Indeed, they sound more like a rushing breeze than a propeller, making a much less intrusive sound. Anecdotally, according to the team, a drone running these props makes a level of sound roughly as annoying as a regular drone about twice as far away. Have a listen in the video below:

> The toroidal propeller, one of the Lab's 【40†@RD100Awards†twitter.com】 winners, has a unique, closed-form propeller design that makes it a significantly quieter alternative to common multirotor propellers on commercial uncrewed aerial vehicles. 【41†https://t.co/hgda3NgYIz†t.co】 【42†pic.twitter.com/5XkIxNVPHd†t.co】
> 
> — Lincoln Laboratory (@MITLL) 【43†January 6, 2023†twitter.com】

"The key thing that we thought was making the propellers quieter, was the fact that you're now distributing the vortices that are being generated by the propeller across the whole shape of it, instead of just at the tip," says Sebastian. "Which then makes it effectively dissipate faster in the atmosphere. That vortex doesn't propagate as far, so you're less likely to hear it."

Propeller noise can be somewhat addressed by placing rings of acoustic treatment around the circumference of a prop's path, which can also act as prop guards from a safety perspective. But these add parasitic mass, reducing battery life, and they can also catch the wind in outdoor situations, making the drone work harder to stay stable. 

The team analyzed these weird-looking toroidal props to see whether there would be a thrust efficiency penalty. Apparently not: the team's best-performing B160 design was not only quieter at a given thrust level than the best standard propeller they tested, it also produced more thrust at a given power level – pretty remarkable given that standard props have more than a century of development behind them and these toroids are at a very early stage, with plenty of optimization yet to come. 

[Image 12: While the MIT team hasn't spent much time optimizing these weird-looking props for efficiency, they're already producing more thrust for a given power level than standard DJI propellers] 

While the MIT team hasn't spent much time optimizing these weird-looking props for efficiency, they're already producing more thrust for a given power level than standard DJI propellers 

MIT Lincoln Laboratory

What's more, their looped shape not only adds structural stability, but decreases the chance of a prop cutting, clipping or catching on things it runs into. You're still not going to want them hitting you in the face, but there's probably a marginal safety improvement there.

In terms of drawbacks, these are fairly complex shapes, so they're much harder to manufacture than standard props using cheap and easy injection molding. They're probably the sort of thing you need to get 3D printed. But even if they double or triple the price of propellers, these are a low-cost part of a drone and the overall impact might not be that tough on the hip pocket. 

It's unclear at this stage whether designs like this might be relevant at a larger scale, replacing traditional propellers on fixed-wing aircraft, or indeed on electric VTOL air taxis. The latter already appear to be significantly quieter than helicopters, but if they end up flooding the urban airspace with fast, cheap, green aerial transport, every decibel of noise will count when it comes to public and regulatory resistance. The question there, really, is what kind of frequencies these larger props will occupy in the audio spectrum, and whether the toroidal props shift the sound in a human-friendly direction. 

The team has patented the design, and while it's not clear whether there are plans to commercialize it, MIT appears to be prepared to license it to interested manufacturers.

### Recommended videos for you

This is crucial, as propellers that are designed to give the highest possible top speed often struggle at low to medium revs, and vice versa. So how is Sharrow Engineering claiming to have cracked the conundrum that has stymied so many others?

### Tip troubles

As ever it seems to be a combination of inspiration and perspiration. The inspiration came from its inventor and CEO of Sharrow Engineering, Greg Sharrow, a music graduate, who originally set out to solve a very different problem.

He wanted to use 【46†camera drones†www.yachtingworld.com】 to film performers in action but soon found that their microphones would pick up the noise of the drones. He realised that most of this noise was not being created by the drone’s tiny electric motors but by the propeller tip vortices.

[Image 3: Propeller-tip-vortices-credit-Rachel-Sloman-flickr]

Visible tip vortices on an aeroplane propeller. Photo: Rachel Sloman / Flickr

These swirling pockets of turbulence are caused by high-pressure air on one side of the blade rushing round to meet the low pressure air on the other, creating induced drag, noise and vibration. The same principle applies to boat propellers, where the tip vortices are even more pronounced and can lead to cavitation, when water is momentarily vapourised by the sudden change in pressure creating bubbles.

Greg reasoned that if he could reduce or even eliminate these tip vortices, it should lead to a quieter, more efficient drone. His light bulb moment came on a dog walk when the idea of a tipless blade, that loops round to rejoin the propeller hub like a strip of twisted ribbon, first popped into his head.

It took a further seven years of intensive research and development, substantial investment, 23 worldwide patents and a switch in focus from drones to boats before Sharrow Engineering unveiled its first production toroidal boat propeller at the 【25†Miami Boat Show】 in February.

Since then it has already won an award for innovation and the company says it is now in discussion with a number of major propeller and engine manufacturers.

It has also modelled and simulated tests on toroidal boat propellers up to 9.87m in diameter for 【49†displacement trawler yachts】, container ships and even super tankers, all of which have shown similar theoretical efficiency gains.
