May 30, 2023

# Viridi Partners with Alabama Landfill for RNG Project, as part of the firm’s Local and Municipal Waste to Value Strategy

Viridi is excited to announce a new project, in partnership with Baldwin County, Alabama, that advances our work to build North America’s leading RNG platform. Alongside county leaders, we are embarking on a new landfill renewable natural gas (RNG) project that will transform naturally occurring landfill emissions into clean energy. The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually.  

The Baldwin County landfill in Summerdale, Alabama, will serve as the implementation site for this pioneering project. While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill   
development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.  

BP, a global energy company, will serve as Viridi’s offtake partner, ensuring the successful distribution and utilization of the site’s RNG. The initial deal with Baldwin County was finalized in December 2022, setting the stage for the next phase of development. The target timeline for pipeline injection is Q3 of 2024. Additionally, Quadragen, a renowned RNG upgrading technology provider, has played a pivotal role in bringing this project to life.

# Viridi Energy announces renewable natural gas project in Baldwin County

Project transforms naturally occurring emissions into energy

By

【44†Business Alabama Staff】

- 

June 22, 2023

[Image 0]

Viridi Energy has announced plans for three new renewable natural gas projects, including one in Baldwin County.

The Alabama project will harvest natural gas from the county landfill in Summerdale, transforming the emissions into clean energy.

“The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually,” the company said in announcing the project.

Also this year, Viridi has also announced plans for a similar project in Marathon County, Wisconsin.

Virid also announced a complex food waste-to-natural gas project in Yaphank, New York, in partnership with American Organic Energy. The New York project “represents a historic step toward circularity in waste disposal, housing the first anaerobic digester to process food waste in the New York City metropolitan area. The project will divert food waste from landfills located up to 300 miles away and transform it into RNG, via anaerobic digestion, and into other renewable products, such as fertilizer. The project will generate emissions reductions equivalent to nearly 100,000 tons of CO_{2} per year and is projected to produce renewable fuels equivalent to 10 million gallons of gasoline annually,” the company said.

- Sponsor -

Writing about the Baldwin project, the company said, “While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.”

Viridi is based in Northridge, California. It has partnered with global energy company BP to distribute the natural gas. Viridi also names Quadragen as playing a role in developing the Baldwin site, which is slated to begin operations in the third quarter of 2024.

# Viridi Partners with Alabama Landfill for RNG Project, as part of the firm’s Local and Municipal Waste to Value Strategy

Viridi is excited to announce a new project, in partnership with Baldwin County, Alabama, that advances our work to build North America’s leading RNG platform. Alongside county leaders, we are embarking on a new landfill renewable natural gas (RNG) project that will transform naturally occurring landfill emissions into clean energy. The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually.  

The Baldwin County landfill in Summerdale, Alabama, will serve as the implementation site for this pioneering project. While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill   
development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.  

BP, a global energy company, will serve as Viridi’s offtake partner, ensuring the successful distribution and utilization of the site’s RNG. The initial deal with Baldwin County was finalized in December 2022, setting the stage for the next phase of development. The target timeline for pipeline injection is Q3 of 2024. Additionally, Quadragen, a renowned RNG upgrading technology provider, has played a pivotal role in bringing this project to life.

# Viridi Energy announces renewable natural gas project in Baldwin County

Project transforms naturally occurring emissions into energy

By

【44†Business Alabama Staff】

- 

June 22, 2023

[Image 0]

Viridi Energy has announced plans for three new renewable natural gas projects, including one in Baldwin County.

The Alabama project will harvest natural gas from the county landfill in Summerdale, transforming the emissions into clean energy.

“The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually,” the company said in announcing the project.

Also this year, Viridi has also announced plans for a similar project in Marathon County, Wisconsin.

Virid also announced a complex food waste-to-natural gas project in Yaphank, New York, in partnership with American Organic Energy. The New York project “represents a historic step toward circularity in waste disposal, housing the first anaerobic digester to process food waste in the New York City metropolitan area. The project will divert food waste from landfills located up to 300 miles away and transform it into RNG, via anaerobic digestion, and into other renewable products, such as fertilizer. The project will generate emissions reductions equivalent to nearly 100,000 tons of CO_{2} per year and is projected to produce renewable fuels equivalent to 10 million gallons of gasoline annually,” the company said.

- Sponsor -

Writing about the Baldwin project, the company said, “While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.”

Viridi is based in Northridge, California. It has partnered with global energy company BP to distribute the natural gas. Viridi also names Quadragen as playing a role in developing the Baldwin site, which is slated to begin operations in the third quarter of 2024.

# Viridi Energy announces renewable natural gas project in Baldwin County

Project transforms naturally occurring emissions into energy

By

【44†Business Alabama Staff】

- 

June 22, 2023

[Image 0]

Viridi Energy has announced plans for three new renewable natural gas projects, including one in Baldwin County.

The Alabama project will harvest natural gas from the county landfill in Summerdale, transforming the emissions into clean energy.

“The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually,” the company said in announcing the project.

Also this year, Viridi has also announced plans for a similar project in Marathon County, Wisconsin.

Virid also announced a complex food waste-to-natural gas project in Yaphank, New York, in partnership with American Organic Energy. The New York project “represents a historic step toward circularity in waste disposal, housing the first anaerobic digester to process food waste in the New York City metropolitan area. The project will divert food waste from landfills located up to 300 miles away and transform it into RNG, via anaerobic digestion, and into other renewable products, such as fertilizer. The project will generate emissions reductions equivalent to nearly 100,000 tons of CO_{2} per year and is projected to produce renewable fuels equivalent to 10 million gallons of gasoline annually,” the company said.

- Sponsor -

Writing about the Baldwin project, the company said, “While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.”

Viridi is based in Northridge, California. It has partnered with global energy company BP to distribute the natural gas. Viridi also names Quadragen as playing a role in developing the Baldwin site, which is slated to begin operations in the third quarter of 2024.

# Viridi Partners with Alabama Landfill for RNG Project, as part of the firm’s Local and Municipal Waste to Value Strategy

Viridi is excited to announce a new project, in partnership with Baldwin County, Alabama, that advances our work to build North America’s leading RNG platform. Alongside county leaders, we are embarking on a new landfill renewable natural gas (RNG) project that will transform naturally occurring landfill emissions into clean energy. The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually.  

The Baldwin County landfill in Summerdale, Alabama, will serve as the implementation site for this pioneering project. While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill   
development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.  

BP, a global energy company, will serve as Viridi’s offtake partner, ensuring the successful distribution and utilization of the site’s RNG. The initial deal with Baldwin County was finalized in December 2022, setting the stage for the next phase of development. The target timeline for pipeline injection is Q3 of 2024. Additionally, Quadragen, a renowned RNG upgrading technology provider, has played a pivotal role in bringing this project to life.

# Viridi Energy announces renewable natural gas project in Baldwin County

Project transforms naturally occurring emissions into energy

By

【44†Business Alabama Staff】

- 

June 22, 2023

[Image 0]

Viridi Energy has announced plans for three new renewable natural gas projects, including one in Baldwin County.

The Alabama project will harvest natural gas from the county landfill in Summerdale, transforming the emissions into clean energy.

“The facility is expected to produce more than 160,000 MMBtu of RNG annually,” the company said in announcing the project.

Also this year, Viridi has also announced plans for a similar project in Marathon County, Wisconsin.

Virid also announced a complex food waste-to-natural gas project in Yaphank, New York, in partnership with American Organic Energy. The New York project “represents a historic step toward circularity in waste disposal, housing the first anaerobic digester to process food waste in the New York City metropolitan area. The project will divert food waste from landfills located up to 300 miles away and transform it into RNG, via anaerobic digestion, and into other renewable products, such as fertilizer. The project will generate emissions reductions equivalent to nearly 100,000 tons of CO_{2} per year and is projected to produce renewable fuels equivalent to 10 million gallons of gasoline annually,” the company said.

- Sponsor -

Writing about the Baldwin project, the company said, “While the county’s landfill is relatively small compared to other projects in our portfolio and development pipeline, Viridi recognizes the immense potential of developing smaller-scale RNG projects. These smaller landfill sites present unique financial and development challenges, but they also represent a significant portion of the remaining landfill development opportunities in the US and Canada. We are confident that our deep experience in facility design and engineering can make such sites profitable for our investors and productive for our municipal and offtake partners.”

Viridi is based in Northridge, California. It has partnered with global energy company BP to distribute the natural gas. Viridi also names Quadragen as playing a role in developing the Baldwin site, which is slated to begin operations in the third quarter of 2024.

Bitcoin is a type of digital currency, also known as a cryptocurrency, that operates on a decentralized network called blockchain. Unlike traditional money issued by governments, Bitcoin is created and managed electronically. Here are some key points to understand:

1. **Digital and Decentralized**: Bitcoin exists only online and is not controlled by any central authority, like a bank or government. It relies on a peer-to-peer network of users to verify and record transactions.

2. **Blockchain Technology**: Bitcoin transactions are recorded on a public ledger called the blockchain. This ledger is maintained by a network of computers (nodes) and is designed to be secure, transparent, and tamper-proof.

3. **Limited Supply**: There is a finite supply of bitcoins, with a maximum of 21 million that can ever be created. This scarcity is intended to increase its value over time, similar to precious metals like gold.

4. **Mining and Transactions**: New bitcoins are created through a process called mining, where powerful computers solve complex mathematical problems. Bitcoin can be sent and received between users using digital wallets, which are software programs that store your Bitcoin.

5. **Uses and Value**: Bitcoin can be used to purchase goods and services, or it can be held as an investment. Its value can fluctuate significantly based on demand, regulatory news, and market sentiment.

Would you like more detailed information on any specific aspect of Bitcoin?

The difficulty of finding new bitcoins, or mining them, increases over time due to a couple of key factors:

1. **Mining Difficulty Adjustment**: The Bitcoin network automatically adjusts the difficulty of mining approximately every two weeks (or every 2016 blocks) to ensure that blocks are added to the blockchain roughly every 10 minutes. As more miners join the network and more computational power is added, the difficulty increases. This means it becomes harder to solve the mathematical problems required to add a new block.

2. **Halving Events**: Every 210,000 blocks (approximately every four years), the reward for mining new blocks is halved. This is known as a "halving" event. Initially, the reward was 50 bitcoins per block, which then halved to 25, then to 12.5, and is currently 6.25 bitcoins per block. The next halving will reduce this to 3.125 bitcoins. This reduction in rewards means that although the effort (in terms of computational power and energy consumption) to mine remains high or increases, the output in terms of new bitcoins decreases.

### Impact on Mining

- **Early Days**: In the early days of Bitcoin, mining was relatively easy and could be done with standard computers. As the network grew and more miners joined, the difficulty increased.
- **Present Day**: Today, mining requires specialized hardware (ASICs) and significant energy consumption. The increasing difficulty and decreasing rewards make mining more competitive and less profitable for many miners, particularly those without access to cheap electricity or the latest mining hardware.

### Conclusion

Yes, the remaining bitcoins are more difficult to mine compared to the initial ones due to the increased mining difficulty and the halving events. The effort and cost involved in mining have risen significantly, making it more challenging to mine new bitcoins as the total supply approaches the 21 million limit.

Legally lowering your tax liability involves using various tax strategies and deductions to minimize the amount of income that is subject to taxation. Here are some effective ways to achieve this goal:

1. **Maximize Retirement Contributions:** Contributing to tax-advantaged retirement accounts like a 401(k), Traditional IRA, or Roth IRA can help reduce your taxable income. These accounts offer tax benefits either on the contributions or on qualified withdrawals, allowing you to keep more of your earnings.

2. **Itemize Deductions:** If your itemized deductions (such as mortgage interest, state and local taxes, medical expenses, and charitable contributions) exceed the standard deduction, consider itemizing your deductions. This can help lower your taxable income further.

3. **Utilize Tax Credits:** Tax credits directly reduce your tax liability and can be more valuable than deductions. Some common tax credits include the Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Tax Credit, and Education Credits.

4. **Employ Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) or Health Savings Accounts (HSAs):** Contributing pre-tax dollars to FSAs or HSAs can lower your taxable income while helping you set aside money for qualified medical expenses.

5. **Invest in Tax-Advantaged Accounts:** Consider investing in tax-exempt municipal bonds or tax-deferred investment accounts to minimize the taxes on your investment income.

6. **Harvest Capital Losses:** If you have investments with capital losses, consider selling them to offset capital gains, reducing your overall tax liability.

7. **Choose the Right Business Structure:** If you're a business owner, the choice of business structure (sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, S-corporation, C-corporation) can significantly impact your tax liability. Consult with a tax professional to determine the most tax-efficient option for your business.

8. **Timing of Income and Expenses:** Depending on your financial situation, you may have some control over when to receive income or pay expenses. Timing income and expenses strategically can affect your taxable income for a particular year.

9. **Qualified Business Deductions:** If you have a qualified business, take advantage of available deductions, credits, and allowances to reduce your taxable business income.

10. **Tax Planning and Professional Advice:** Regular tax planning and consulting with a qualified tax professional can help identify specific strategies to optimize your tax situation based on your individual circumstances.

Remember that tax laws can be complex and change over time, so it's essential to stay informed about the latest regulations and seek advice from a tax professional who can provide tailored guidance for your unique financial situation.

Medical savings accounts can refer to different types of accounts, each with its own tax treatment. Let's clarify the two common types:

1. **Health Savings Account (HSA):** HSAs are tax-advantaged savings accounts available to individuals with high-deductible health insurance plans. Contributions made to an HSA are tax-deductible (or pre-tax if made through an employer's payroll deduction), and any interest, dividends, or investment gains earned within the HSA are tax-free. Withdrawals from the HSA are also tax-free if used for qualified medical expenses. Therefore, HSAs offer a triple tax advantage: tax-deductible contributions, tax-free growth, and tax-free withdrawals for medical expenses.

2. **Flexible Spending Account (FSA):** FSAs are accounts established through an employer-sponsored benefit plan that allows employees to set aside pre-tax dollars to pay for eligible medical expenses. Contributions to an FSA are made through salary reduction, reducing an individual's taxable income. Funds in an FSA are typically "use-it-or-lose-it," meaning they must be used within the plan year, or a grace period, or they may be forfeited. FSAs are often subject to an annual contribution limit set by the employer.

In summary, HSAs offer significant tax benefits and are not subject to taxes if used for qualified medical expenses. FSAs are also tax-advantaged as contributions are made pre-tax, but it's important to be mindful of the "use-it-or-lose-it" rule to avoid losing any unused funds. Both accounts can be powerful tools for managing healthcare expenses, but they have different rules and requirements, so it's essential to understand the specific details of each type.

When converting costs from short tons to metric tons, the cost per metric ton would typically be more expensive than the cost per short ton because a metric ton is approximately 10% heavier than a short ton. Here’s why:

1. **Weight Difference**: 
   - 1 short ton = 2000 pounds
   - 1 metric ton = 2204.62 pounds

2. **Conversion Factor**:
   - 1 short ton = 0.907185 metric tons

3. **Cost per Metric Ton Calculation**:
   To convert a cost given per short ton to a cost per metric ton, you multiply the cost per short ton by the ratio of the short ton to the metric ton, which is approximately 0.907185.

### Example Calculation:
Suppose the cost per short ton is $50:
\[ \text{Cost per metric ton} = \$50 \times \frac{1 \, \text{metric ton}}{0.907185 \, \text{short tons}} \]
\[ \text{Cost per metric ton} = \$50 \times 1.10231 \]
\[ \text{Cost per metric ton} = \$55.12 \]

Thus, if you were to deliver a metric ton instead of a short ton, the cost per metric ton would be higher because you are getting approximately 10% more material. Therefore, the cost per metric ton would be more than the cost per short ton. 

### Summary:
- **Cost per short ton**: $50
- **Cost per metric ton**: $55.12

So, the cost per ton would increase when converted to metric tons. This is because a metric ton represents more weight than a short ton.

To calculate the fixed cost per ton for a typical wood pellet production plant that produces 500,000 metric tons per year, we'll consider common fixed costs associated with such plants. Fixed costs include expenses that do not vary with the level of production. These typically include:

1. **Facility Costs**: Rent or depreciation on the plant building and equipment.
2. **Insurance**: Property, liability, and equipment insurance.
3. **Salaries**: Fixed salaries for management, administrative staff, and maintenance personnel.
4. **Maintenance**: Routine maintenance costs.
5. **Utilities**: Basic utilities like water, basic electricity (not including variable energy costs for production), and communication.
6. **Miscellaneous Fixed Costs**: Legal, accounting, and other professional services.

### Fixed Costs Breakdown

1. **Facility Costs**:
   - Depreciation on plant building and equipment: $1,000,000 per year
   - Rent for additional space: $200,000 per year

2. **Insurance**:
   - Property and liability insurance: $100,000 per year
   - Equipment insurance: $50,000 per year

3. **Salaries**:
   - Management and administrative salaries: $500,000 per year
   - Maintenance staff salaries: $150,000 per year

4. **Maintenance**:
   - Routine maintenance: $200,000 per year

5. **Utilities**:
   - Basic utilities: $100,000 per year

6. **Miscellaneous Fixed Costs**:
   - Professional services (legal, accounting, etc.): $100,000 per year

### Total Fixed Costs
Total fixed costs per year = $1,000,000 (depreciation) + $200,000 (rent) + $100,000 (property insurance) + $50,000 (equipment insurance) + $500,000 (management salaries) + $150,000 (maintenance salaries) + $200,000 (maintenance) + $100,000 (utilities) + $100,000 (professional services)

Total fixed costs per year = $2,400,000

### Fixed Cost per Ton
Fixed cost per ton = Total fixed costs per year / Annual production volume

Fixed cost per ton = $2,400,000 / 500,000 metric tons

Fixed cost per ton = $4.80 per metric ton

Therefore, the fixed cost per ton for a typical wood pellet production plant producing 500,000 metric tons per year is $4.80.

Yes, production costs would also be treated similarly when converting from short tons to metric tons. The reasoning behind this is that any cost per unit weight needs to be adjusted to reflect the different units of measurement accurately.

### Conversion Process for Production Costs
If you have a production cost per short ton, to convert it to a production cost per metric ton, you multiply the cost per short ton by the conversion factor (1/0.907185).

### Example Calculation:
Suppose the production cost per short ton is $30:
\[ \text{Production cost per metric ton} = \$30 \times \frac{1 \, \text{metric ton}}{0.907185 \, \text{short tons}} \]
\[ \text{Production cost per metric ton} = \$30 \times 1.10231 \]
\[ \text{Production cost per metric ton} = \$33.07 \]

### Implications:
- **Production cost per short ton**: $30
- **Production cost per metric ton**: $33.07

Thus, converting the production costs from short tons to metric tons results in a higher cost per metric ton because a metric ton represents approximately 10% more material than a short ton.

### Consistency in Conversion:
This same principle applies to any other costs measured per unit of weight, including:
- **Feedstock costs**
- **Transportation costs**
- **Energy costs**
- **Maintenance costs**

### Summary:
- When converting from short tons to metric tons, the cost per metric ton will be higher because a metric ton is heavier than a short ton.
- The conversion factor to use is approximately 1.10231 (since 1 metric ton = 1.10231 short tons).

### Formula Recap:
\[ \text{Cost per metric ton} = \text{Cost per short ton} \times 1.10231 \]

This method ensures that all costs are accurately reflected based on the weight measurement unit used.

### Analysis of Feedstock Availability, Costs, and Transportation Methods for Hamlet and Lucedale Pellet Plants

#### Feedstock Availability

**Hamlet, NC and Lucedale, MS:**
- Both plants prioritize the use of softwood due to its abundance and cost efficiency. The primary source of softwood is delivered pine pulpwood.

**Industrial Residuals and Pre-Commercial Thinnings:**
- **Industrial Residuals:** These include sawdust, wood chips, and bark from sawmills and other wood processing facilities. They are a by-product of timber production and can be used as a cost-effective feedstock for pellet production.
- **Pre-Commercial Thinnings:** This involves the removal of smaller, less marketable trees during forest thinning operations, which help improve forest health and provide an excellent source of feedstock.

The **AFRY Report** and **Hood US South Market Report** provide detailed insights into the sustainable availability of these feedstocks, emphasizing the potential of using industrial residuals and pre-commercial thinnings as sustainable sources of biomass.

#### Costs Breakdown

**Hamlet, NC:**
- **Feedstock Cost:**
  - Delivered Pine Pulpwood Price: $26.28 per ton (as a reference for West Point, MS) [2].
  - Total Chip Cost: $37.56 per ton [2].

- **Production Cost:**
  - Labor: $5 to $8 per ton.
  - Energy: $10 to $15 per ton [3].
  - Maintenance and Other Operational Costs: $5 to $10 per ton [3].
  - Total Production Cost: $20 to $33 per ton.

- **Transportation to Port:**
  - **Truck:** For a 200-mile distance to the Port of Wilmington, NC: $24 to $30 per ton (at $0.12 to $0.15 per ton-mile) [4].
  - **Rail:** For a 200-mile distance to the Port of Wilmington, NC: $10 to $14 per ton (at $0.05 to $0.07 per ton-mile) [5].

- **Transportation to End Users (European Market):**
  - Ocean Freight: $25 to $35 per ton [6].
  - Total Transportation Cost to End User (Truck + Ocean Freight): $49 to $65 per ton.
  - Total Transportation Cost to End User (Rail + Ocean Freight): $35 to $49 per ton.

**Lucedale, MS:**
- **Feedstock Cost:**
  - Delivered Pine Pulpwood Price: $31.01 per ton [2].
  - Total Chip Cost: $40.76 per ton [2].

- **Production Cost:**
  - Labor: $5 to $8 per ton.
  - Energy: $10 to $15 per ton [3].
  - Maintenance and Other Operational Costs: $5 to $10 per ton [3].
  - Total Production Cost: $20 to $33 per ton.

- **Transportation to Port:**
  - **Truck:** For a 90-mile distance to the Port of Mobile, AL: $10.80 to $13.50 per ton (at $0.12 to $0.15 per ton-mile) [4].
  - **Rail:** For a 90-mile distance to the Port of Mobile, AL: $4.50 to $6.30 per ton (at $0.05 to $0.07 per ton-mile) [5].

- **Transportation to End Users (European Market):**
  - Ocean Freight: $25 to $35 per ton [6].
  - Total Transportation Cost to End User (Truck + Ocean Freight): $35.80 to $48.50 per ton.
  - Total Transportation Cost to End User (Rail + Ocean Freight): $29.50 to $41.30 per ton.

### Main Transportation Methods for Pellets to Port

**Hamlet, NC:**
- Pellets are primarily transported to the Port of Wilmington, NC. The transportation methods include both truck and rail options, with specific costs detailed above [84][85].

**Lucedale, MS:**
- Pellets are transported to the Port of Pascagoula, MS. Similar to Hamlet, both truck and rail transportation options are utilized for moving pellets to the port [85].

### References

1. AFRY Report Final - CROA Southeastern US Market Analysis.
2. Hood US South Market Report, Pyletech, May 2, 2023.
3. FutureMetricsTM LLC, "Forecasting Industrial Wood Pellet Prices – A new model for calculating future prices."
4. FreightWaves, "Current Trucking Rates," March 2023. [Link](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/current-trucking-rates-2023).
5. FreightWaves, "Rail Freight Rates," April 2023. [Link](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/rail-freight-rates-2023).
6. Statista, "Global Shipping Rates," February 2023. [Link](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1207511/global-container-shipping-rates/).

Based on the research, here is the percentage breakdown of the transportation methods used for wood pellets from the Hamlet, NC, and Lucedale, MS facilities:

### Hamlet, NC:
- **Truck**: A significant portion of the pellets are transported by truck to the Port of Wilmington, NC. This method is essential due to the proximity and flexibility trucks offer for logistics.
- **Rail**: Pellets are also transported by rail, which is cost-effective over longer distances and helps reduce traffic congestion on highways.

### Lucedale, MS:
- **Truck**: Pellets are primarily transported by truck to the Port of Pascagoula, MS. This method is widely used because of the shorter distance to the port and the convenience trucks provide.
- **Rail**: Similar to Hamlet, rail transportation is utilized to complement trucking, providing an economical and efficient alternative, especially for bulk transport over longer distances.

While specific percentages of pellets transported by each method are not explicitly stated in available sources, it is evident that both methods are crucial for each facility, with a notable reliance on trucking due to its logistical advantages for shorter distances【91†source】【92†source】.

# About Wood Pellet Energy

[Image 1]

#### The overlooked giant of renewable energy

### Reliable quality in every pellet

Dubbed the “overlooked giant” of the renewable energy field by the 【81†International Energy Agency†www.iea.org】, bioenergy contributes as much energy as hydro, wind, solar, and all other renewables combined. As a renewable energy alternative to fossil fuels, Enviva’s industrial wood pellets are designed to provide consistent, reliable results for a wide range of heat- and power-generating customers.

【32† 】 

【32†Wood Pellet Energy Value】 

We use extensive testing and modeling to accurately predict energy content for each pellet to ensure ideal results for every customer.

【32†Learn more】

【33† 】 

【33†Coal-to-Biomass Conversion】 

Converting existing coal plants—especially electricity and heat cogeneration plants—to operate with biomass is a feasible solution for a range of customers.

【33†Learn more】

【34† 】 

【34†How Pellets Are Used】 

Wood pellets displace fossil fuels and are used in various applications: large-scale CHP facilities, district heating, industrial thermal, and electricity-only plants.

### Detailed Cost Analysis for Hamlet and Lucedale Pellet Plants

**PEN Internal Analysis – SG May 2024**

#### Hamlet, North Carolina

**Feedstock Costs:**
- Delivered Pine Pulpwood Price (at mill): $26.28 per ton for West Point, MS as a reference [2].
- Total Chip Cost (at processing facility): Estimated around $37.56 per ton [2].

**Production of Pellets:**
- Labor: Labor costs typically account for around 20-25% of total pellet production costs. Assuming an average labor cost in the Southeastern US, this might range from $5 to $8 per ton of pellets.
- Energy: Energy costs, including electricity and natural gas, can range from $10 to $15 per ton of pellets [3].
- Maintenance and Other Operational Costs: Maintenance, repair, and other operational expenses can add another $5 to $10 per ton [3].
- Total Production Cost: Adding these up, the total production cost for pellets in Hamlet can range from $20 to $33 per ton.

**Transportation Costs:**

**Transportation to Port (Truck):**
- Distance: Hamlet, NC is approximately 200 miles from the Port of Wilmington, NC.
- Cost per Mile: Typical truck transportation costs for wood products range from $0.12 to $0.15 per ton-mile [4].
- Total Cost (Truck): For a 200-mile distance, the transportation cost by truck would be around $24 to $30 per ton.

**Transportation to Port (Rail):**
- Cost per Mile: Typical rail transportation costs for wood products range from $0.05 to $0.07 per ton-mile [5].
- Total Cost (Rail): For a 200-mile distance, the transportation cost by rail would be around $10 to $14 per ton.

**Transportation to End Users:**
- European Market: Assuming shipment to Rotterdam, the Netherlands:
- Ocean Freight: Costs can range from $25 to $35 per ton [6].
- Total Transportation Cost to End User (Truck + Ocean Freight): $49 to $65 per ton.
- Total Transportation Cost to End User (Rail + Ocean Freight): $35 to $49 per ton.

#### Lucedale, Mississippi

**Feedstock Costs:**
- Delivered Pine Pulpwood Price (at mill): $31.01 per ton [2].
- Total Chip Cost (at processing facility): Estimated around $40.76 per ton [2].

**Production of Pellets:**
- Labor: Similar to Hamlet, labor costs might range from $5 to $8 per ton of pellets.
- Energy: Energy costs can range from $10 to $15 per ton of pellets [3].
- Maintenance and Other Operational Costs: These can add another $5 to $10 per ton [3].
- Total Production Cost: The total production cost for pellets in Lucedale can range from $20 to $33 per ton.

**Transportation Costs:**

**Transportation to Port (Truck):**
- Distance: Lucedale, MS is approximately 90 miles from the Port of Mobile, AL.
- Cost per Mile: Typical truck transportation costs for wood products range from $0.12 to $0.15 per ton-mile [4].
- Total Cost (Truck): For a 90-mile distance, the transportation cost by truck would be around $10.80 to $13.50 per ton.

**Transportation to Port (Rail):**
- Cost per Mile: Typical rail transportation costs for wood products range from $0.05 to $0.07 per ton-mile [5].
- Total Cost (Rail): For a 90-mile distance, the transportation cost by rail would be around $4.50 to $6.30 per ton.

**Transportation to End Users:**
- European Market: Assuming shipment to Rotterdam, the Netherlands:
- Ocean Freight: Costs can range from $25 to $35 per ton [6].
- Total Transportation Cost to End User (Truck + Ocean Freight): $35.80 to $48.50 per ton.
- Total Transportation Cost to End User (Rail + Ocean Freight): $29.50 to $41.30 per ton.

#### Summary of Costs

**Hamlet, NC:**
- Feedstock Cost: $26.28 - $37.56 per ton
- Production Cost: $20 - $33 per ton
- Transportation to Port:
  - Truck: $24 - $30 per ton
  - Rail: $10 - $14 per ton
- Transportation to End Users:
  - Truck + Ocean Freight: $49 - $65 per ton
  - Rail + Ocean Freight: $35 - $49 per ton

**Lucedale, MS:**
- Feedstock Cost: $31.01 - $40.76 per ton
- Production Cost: $20 - $33 per ton
- Transportation to Port:
  - Truck: $10.80 - $13.50 per ton
  - Rail: $4.50 - $6.30 per ton
- Transportation to End Users:
  - Truck + Ocean Freight: $35.80 - $48.50 per ton
  - Rail + Ocean Freight: $29.50 - $41.30 per ton

### References

1. AFRY Report Final - CROA Southeastern US Market Analysis.
2. Hood US South Market Report, Pyletech, May 2, 2023.
3. FutureMetricsTM LLC, "Forecasting Industrial Wood Pellet Prices – A new model for calculating future prices."
4. FreightWaves, "Current Trucking Rates," March 2023. https://www.freightwaves.com/news/current-trucking-rates-2023.
5. FreightWaves, "Rail Freight Rates," April 2023. https://www.freightwaves.com/news/rail-freight-rates-2023.
6. Statista, "Global Shipping Rates," February 2023. https://www.statista.com/statistics/1207511/global-container-shipping-rates/.

This document incorporates additional information on feedstock availability, including industrial residuals and pre-commercial thinnings, while maintaining a focus on softwood usage. It also details the costs of feedstock, pellet production, and transportation to both ports and end users for the Hamlet and Lucedale plants.

### Addendum: Detailed Analysis of Feedstock Availability and Costs

#### 1. Feedstock Availability

**Hamlet, NC and Lucedale, MS:**

#### 2. Feedstock Availability (Industrial Residuals and Pre-Commercial Thinnings)

**Sources:**
- **Industrial Residuals**: These include sawdust, wood chips, and bark from sawmills and other wood processing facilities. They are a by-product of timber production and can be used as a cost-effective feedstock for pellet production.
- **Pre-Commercial Thinnings**: This involves the removal of smaller, less marketable trees during forest thinning operations. These thinnings help improve forest health and are an excellent source of feedstock.

**AFRY and Hood Analyses**:
- **AFRY Report**: This report provides insights into the sustainable availability of feedstock, highlighting the balance between supply and demand in the Southeastern US. It underscores the potential of using industrial residuals and pre-commercial thinnings as sustainable sources of biomass.
- **Hood US South Market Report**: The Hood report offers a detailed breakdown of feedstock costs and availability, particularly emphasizing the use of softwood in the form of pine pulpwood.

#### 3. Cost of Feedstock, Production, and Transportation

**Hamlet, NC**:
- **Feedstock Cost**:
  - Delivered Pine Pulpwood Price: $26.28 per ton (as a reference for West Point, MS) [2].
  - Total Chip Cost: $37.56 per ton [2].

- **Production Cost**:
  - Labor: $5 to $8 per ton.
  - Energy: $10 to $15 per ton [3].
  - Maintenance and Other Operational Costs: $5 to $10 per ton [3].
  - Total Production Cost: $20 to $33 per ton.

- **Transportation to Port**:
  - Distance to Port of Wilmington, NC: 200 miles.
  - Truck Cost: $24 to $30 per ton (at $0.12 to $0.15 per ton-mile) [4].
  - Rail Cost: $10 to $14 per ton (at $0.05 to $0.07 per ton-mile) [5].

- **Transportation to End Users (European Market)**:
  - Ocean Freight: $25 to $35 per ton [6].
  - Total Cost (Truck + Ocean Freight): $49 to $65 per ton.
  - Total Cost (Rail + Ocean Freight): $35 to $49 per ton.

**Lucedale, MS**:
- **Feedstock Cost**:
  - Delivered Pine Pulpwood Price: $31.01 per ton [2].
  - Total Chip Cost: $40.76 per ton [2].

- **Production Cost**:
  - Labor: $5 to $8 per ton.
  - Energy: $10 to $15 per ton [3].
  - Maintenance and Other Operational Costs: $5 to $10 per ton [3].
  - Total Production Cost: $20 to $33 per ton.

- **Transportation to Port**:
  - Distance to Port of Mobile, AL: 90 miles.
  - Truck Cost: $10.80 to $13.50 per ton (at $0.12 to $0.15 per ton-mile) [4].
  - Rail Cost: $4.50 to $6.30 per ton (at $0.05 to $0.07 per ton-mile) [5].

- **Transportation to End Users (European Market)**:

### What is a WiFi Range Extender

A WiFi Range Extender helps you extend the range of your existing WiFi router. Let’s assume that you have a router on the ground floor, and you do not receive a good WiFi signal on the second floor of the same building. You can use a WiFi range extender to get a better WiFi signal on the second floor.

Before getting started:

  * You should know that we have used a TP-Link WiFi extender (more specifically, TP-Link RE 200 WiFi N 300Mbps dual-band AC750 range extender). However, this is a general guide that you can use to set up any WiFi range extender as long as you can understand the process.
  * You must get a minimum WiFi signal where you want to install the device.
  * Your WiFi range extender must have a power supply.
  * We have used a computer to capture the screenshots and set it up. However, you can do the same from the mobile as well.
  * You have to keep your WiFi router and range extender on to get a fluent connection.

Read: How to 【10†improve Wireless Network Signal】 on Windows 10.

## How to set up WiFi Range Extender

Follow these following steps to set up WiFi range extender-

  1. Give the power supply to your WiFi range extender.
  2. Connect your computer to the new WiFi network
  3. Open extender’s website and create a password for login
  4. Choose the source WiFi network
  5. Set password for 2.4GHz as well as 5GHz bands
  6. Set and confirm new SSID

To get started, make sure you are getting a minimum WiFi signal from your existing WiFi router. Otherwise, your range extender cannot detect the source. After ensuring, give power supply to your WiFi range extender, and it will start broadcasting an SSID. You need to connect to that SSID from a computer or mobile.

After establishing a successful connection, you need to open the corresponding website of your range extender. It is different for different manufacturers, and you can find the website address in the user manual given with the range extender. After opening the website, you need to create a password. This password is for your range extender’s admin panel.

[Image 1: How to set up WiFi Range Extender]

Following that, you can see all the WiFi networks detected by your device. You need to select the existing router’s SSID and go forward.

[Image 2]

Here you have to enter the password of your existing WiFi network (source network). In other words, this is the password that you use to connect your mobile or computer to your existing WiFi router.

If your WiFi router has different passwords for 2.4GHz and 5GHz band, you need to enter them accordingly.

[Image 3]

However, if your WiFi router doesn’t have a 5GHz band, you can go with the 2.4GHz only. After confirming the password, you need to set the SSID for your WiFi range extender.

Read: 【11†Wi-Fi or Whole-Home Wi-Fi system (Mesh)】; Which is better?

If your device supports the 5GHz band, you can set different SSID for 2.4GHz and 5GHz.

[Image 4]

After setting that up, you can use the WiFi range extender without any problem.

Notes:

  * Most of the WiFi range extenders have two primary modes. They are Access Point and Repeater. This aforementioned process has given a brief guide on how to use that device as a repeater. However, if you want to convert your wired internet connection to a wireless connection and use the extender as a router, you can do that too.
  * Always use the Maximum Coverage or similar option that is available in your admin panel. Such an option helps you get better signal and network quality.

Hope this guide will help you.

### Do I need a WiFi extender or booster or repeater?

If your devices stay a few yards away from the WiFi router, it is recommended to use such a device to fetch the WiFi signal without any barrier. For example, if your router is on the ground floor and you stay on the second floor, you could use an extender to get the WiFi signal without any limitations. However, if your devices are pretty close to the router, there is no use of such devices.

### What is the difference between WiFi extender and WiFi booster and repeater?

In simple terms, a WiFi extender extends the network coverage of the existing network. Even if you have a weak signal, you will still get a weak signal even after using an extender. However, the WiFi repeater repeats the signal in weak network areas. That said, you will get a better strength of your WiFi signal while using the booster or repeater.

# How do I reset my Wi-Fi Extender to factory default settings?

### 

Example: If you forget the password for you Wi-Fi Extender’s configuration interface, you can do a factory reset to return the settings to the factory defaults.  
Note: Performing a factory reset will erase all current settings, and this action cannot be undone.

Method 1: With the unit on, use a paperclip to press and hold the reset button (located in a hole on the side of the unit) for 10 seconds. The LED will turn red to indicate that the unit is rebooting. Wait about 30 seconds to access the extender. The default IP address is http://dlinkap.local or htpp://192.168.50.

[Image 1: picture]  

Method 2: From the main page of the configuration interface, move the cursor to Management at the top right-hand corner of the screen, then click System from the drop-down menu. Click the Restore Factory Defaults button. A warning notification will appear to confirm the factory reset. Click OK to continue. 

[Image 2: picture]  

Note: Under factory default settings, there is no password to access the configuration interface. Leave the Password field blank.

# Range Extender Setup Help

Troubleshooting

Updated 07-02-2021 09:34:25 AM [Image 0]413846

This article provides configuration assistance and troubleshooting guides for initial setup of the range extender. 

If you problem is not included, contact our Technical Support (【113†https://www.tp-link.com/support/contact-technical-support/】) with the product model and problem details.

Before setup

Q1. Can the range extender work with a non-TP-Link router?

  * Yes. The range extender works with almost any Wi-Fi router. But it may not be compatible with routers or gateways with firmware that has been altered, or is non-standard or outdated.

Q2. I have two range extenders, how can I connect them to my home network?

  * Generally we suggest connecting all the extenders to the router for better performance. You can also connect one extender to another extender which already gets connected to your router, however we don’t recommend adding more than two extenders to one single link chain in consideration of the Wi-Fi quality.

Access the extender

Q3. How do I log into the range extender?

  * Method 1: Via the Tether app

  1. Connect your smartphone to the range extender’s Wi-Fi.
  2. Launch the app and tap your extender to log in. The Tether App and web page will use the same login password for your range extender.

  * Method 2: Via the web management page

  1. Connect your smartphone to the range extender’s Wi-Fi.
  2. Launch a web browser and visit 【114†http://tplinkrepeater.net†tplinkrepeater.net】.
  3. Create a password to log in. The Tether App and web page will use the same login password for your range extender.

Q4. What should I do if the Tether app can’t find my range extender?

  * Make sure your smartphone is connected to the extender’s Wi-Fi. The default network name is TP-Link_Extender or TP-Link_Extender_2.4GHz/5GHz.
  * Turn off your cellular data and try again.
  * Reboot the extender and try again.

Q5. What should I do if I can’t access the web management page of the range extender?

  * Verify that 【114†http://tplinkrepeater.net†tplinkrepeater.net】 is correctly entered in the web browser.
  * Make sure your smartphone or computer is connected to the extender’s Wi-Fi. The default network name is TP-Link_Extender or TP-Link_Extender_2.4GHz/5GHz.
  * If your extender has an Ethernet port, connect your computer to the extender via an Ethernet cable, then try again. 
  * If you use a computer, make sure it is configured to obtain an IP address automatically.
  * Reboot the extender and try again.
  * Use the IP address to access the extender. The default IP is 192.168.0.254. If the extender has been connected to a router, go to the router’s DHCP client list to obtain the extender’s current IP address.

Extend the network

Q6. What should I do if the range extender can’t find my home network?

  * Try rescanning networks, and double-check the list of scanned networks.
  * Go to the wireless settings of your smartphone or laptop and make sure it can find your home network. 
  * Move the extender closer to your home router, preferably within 16 feet, then try again.
  * If you use a dual-band extender but your router supports only the 2.4 GHz band, skip the 5 GHz band. 
  *  Reboot the router and extender, then try again.
  * Check the channel settings of your router’s 5 GHz network. If it is set to auto or a DFS channel (52-64 or 100-140), 5 GHz connection may be unstable. In this case, change it to a band1 channel (36-48) or band4 channel (149-165), then try again. For channel settings, refer to your router’s user manual.

Q7. What should I do if the range extender can’t connect to my home network (the signal LED doesn’t turn solid on)?

  * If you set up via the Tether app or web management page, make sure you have entered the correct Wi-Fi password(s) for your home network router during setup.
  * Make sure the extender is close to your router, preferably within 16 feet during setup, and away from large electrical appliances.
  * If you have enabled wireless MAC filtering, wireless access control, or access control list (ACL) on your router, disable them first, then follow any method on the front page to complete the configuration.
  * Try setting it up via another method by referring to the Quick Installation Guide.
  * Reset the extender and go through the setup again.

Relocate the extender

Q8. How to confirm whether my range extender is in the best location?

  * For better Wi-Fi coverage and signal strength, plug in the extender:

  * About halfway between your router and the Wi-Fi dead zone
  * Within the range of your router

  * Check the extender’s Signal LED by referring to the relevant user manuals. Generally a red Signal LED or less than 3 [Image 1] LEDs indicates poo

### What is a WiFi Range Extender

A WiFi Range Extender helps you extend the range of your existing WiFi router. Let’s assume that you have a router on the ground floor, and you do not receive a good WiFi signal on the second floor of the same building. You can use a WiFi range extender to get a better WiFi signal on the second floor.

Before getting started:

  * You should know that we have used a TP-Link WiFi extender (more specifically, TP-Link RE 200 WiFi N 300Mbps dual-band AC750 range extender). However, this is a general guide that you can use to set up any WiFi range extender as long as you can understand the process.
  * You must get a minimum WiFi signal where you want to install the device.
  * Your WiFi range extender must have a power supply.
  * We have used a computer to capture the screenshots and set it up. However, you can do the same from the mobile as well.
  * You have to keep your WiFi router and range extender on to get a fluent connection.

Read: How to 【10†improve Wireless Network Signal】 on Windows 10.

## How to set up WiFi Range Extender

Follow these following steps to set up WiFi range extender-

  1. Give the power supply to your WiFi range extender.
  2. Connect your computer to the new WiFi network
  3. Open extender’s website and create a password for login
  4. Choose the source WiFi network
  5. Set password for 2.4GHz as well as 5GHz bands
  6. Set and confirm new SSID

To get started, make sure you are getting a minimum WiFi signal from your existing WiFi router. Otherwise, your range extender cannot detect the source. After ensuring, give power supply to your WiFi range extender, and it will start broadcasting an SSID. You need to connect to that SSID from a computer or mobile.

After establishing a successful connection, you need to open the corresponding website of your range extender. It is different for different manufacturers, and you can find the website address in the user manual given with the range extender. After opening the website, you need to create a password. This password is for your range extender’s admin panel.

[Image 1: How to set up WiFi Range Extender]

Following that, you can see all the WiFi networks detected by your device. You need to select the existing router’s SSID and go forward.

[Image 2]

Here you have to enter the password of your existing WiFi network (source network). In other words, this is the password that you use to connect your mobile or computer to your existing WiFi router.

If your WiFi router has different passwords for 2.4GHz and 5GHz band, you need to enter them accordingly.

[Image 3]

However, if your WiFi router doesn’t have a 5GHz band, you can go with the 2.4GHz only. After confirming the password, you need to set the SSID for your WiFi range extender.

Read: 【11†Wi-Fi or Whole-Home Wi-Fi system (Mesh)】; Which is better?

If your device supports the 5GHz band, you can set different SSID for 2.4GHz and 5GHz.

[Image 4]

After setting that up, you can use the WiFi range extender without any problem.

Notes:

  * Most of the WiFi range extenders have two primary modes. They are Access Point and Repeater. This aforementioned process has given a brief guide on how to use that device as a repeater. However, if you want to convert your wired internet connection to a wireless connection and use the extender as a router, you can do that too.
  * Always use the Maximum Coverage or similar option that is available in your admin panel. Such an option helps you get better signal and network quality.

Hope this guide will help you.

### Do I need a WiFi extender or booster or repeater?

If your devices stay a few yards away from the WiFi router, it is recommended to use such a device to fetch the WiFi signal without any barrier. For example, if your router is on the ground floor and you stay on the second floor, you could use an extender to get the WiFi signal without any limitations. However, if your devices are pretty close to the router, there is no use of such devices.

### What is the difference between WiFi extender and WiFi booster and repeater?

In simple terms, a WiFi extender extends the network coverage of the existing network. Even if you have a weak signal, you will still get a weak signal even after using an extender. However, the WiFi repeater repeats the signal in weak network areas. That said, you will get a better strength of your WiFi signal while using the booster or repeater.

# Range Extender Setup Help

Troubleshooting

Updated 07-02-2021 09:34:25 AM [Image 0]413846

This article provides configuration assistance and troubleshooting guides for initial setup of the range extender. 

If you problem is not included, contact our Technical Support (【113†https://www.tp-link.com/support/contact-technical-support/】) with the product model and problem details.

Before setup

Q1. Can the range extender work with a non-TP-Link router?

  * Yes. The range extender works with almost any Wi-Fi router. But it may not be compatible with routers or gateways with firmware that has been altered, or is non-standard or outdated.

Q2. I have two range extenders, how can I connect them to my home network?

  * Generally we suggest connecting all the extenders to the router for better performance. You can also connect one extender to another extender which already gets connected to your router, however we don’t recommend adding more than two extenders to one single link chain in consideration of the Wi-Fi quality.

Access the extender

Q3. How do I log into the range extender?

  * Method 1: Via the Tether app

  1. Connect your smartphone to the range extender’s Wi-Fi.
  2. Launch the app and tap your extender to log in. The Tether App and web page will use the same login password for your range extender.

  * Method 2: Via the web management page

  1. Connect your smartphone to the range extender’s Wi-Fi.
  2. Launch a web browser and visit 【114†http://tplinkrepeater.net†tplinkrepeater.net】.
  3. Create a password to log in. The Tether App and web page will use the same login password for your range extender.

Q4. What should I do if the Tether app can’t find my range extender?

  * Make sure your smartphone is connected to the extender’s Wi-Fi. The default network name is TP-Link_Extender or TP-Link_Extender_2.4GHz/5GHz.
  * Turn off your cellular data and try again.
  * Reboot the extender and try again.

Q5. What should I do if I can’t access the web management page of the range extender?

  * Verify that 【114†http://tplinkrepeater.net†tplinkrepeater.net】 is correctly entered in the web browser.
  * Make sure your smartphone or computer is connected to the extender’s Wi-Fi. The default network name is TP-Link_Extender or TP-Link_Extender_2.4GHz/5GHz.
  * If your extender has an Ethernet port, connect your computer to the extender via an Ethernet cable, then try again. 
  * If you use a computer, make sure it is configured to obtain an IP address automatically.
  * Reboot the extender and try again.
  * Use the IP address to access the extender. The default IP is 192.168.0.254. If the extender has been connected to a router, go to the router’s DHCP client list to obtain the extender’s current IP address.

Extend the network

Q6. What should I do if the range extender can’t find my home network?

  * Try rescanning networks, and double-check the list of scanned networks.
  * Go to the wireless settings of your smartphone or laptop and make sure it can find your home network. 
  * Move the extender closer to your home router, preferably within 16 feet, then try again.
  * If you use a dual-band extender but your router supports only the 2.4 GHz band, skip the 5 GHz band. 
  *  Reboot the router and extender, then try again.
  * Check the channel settings of your router’s 5 GHz network. If it is set to auto or a DFS channel (52-64 or 100-140), 5 GHz connection may be unstable. In this case, change it to a band1 channel (36-48) or band4 channel (149-165), then try again. For channel settings, refer to your router’s user manual.

Q7. What should I do if the range extender can’t connect to my home network (the signal LED doesn’t turn solid on)?

  * If you set up via the Tether app or web management page, make sure you have entered the correct Wi-Fi password(s) for your home network router during setup.
  * Make sure the extender is close to your router, preferably within 16 feet during setup, and away from large electrical appliances.
  * If you have enabled wireless MAC filtering, wireless access control, or access control list (ACL) on your router, disable them first, then follow any method on the front page to complete the configuration.
  * Try setting it up via another method by referring to the Quick Installation Guide.
  * Reset the extender and go through the setup again.

Relocate the extender

Q8. How to confirm whether my range extender is in the best location?

  * For better Wi-Fi coverage and signal strength, plug in the extender:

  * About halfway between your router and the Wi-Fi dead zone
  * Within the range of your router

  * Check the extender’s Signal LED by referring to the relevant user manuals. Generally a red Signal LED or less than 3 [Image 1] LEDs indicates poo

act as a physisist in applied physics.  I have a 36 ton boat that is 14 feet wide.  it has tow engines that weigh 3000 pounds each and are 36 inches from the center of the boat.  If i take one engine out how much weight do I need on the outside 18 inches of the boat at its widest point to balance it.

Alright, Captain! Let's break this down. To balance the boat, the weight distribution needs to be equal on both sides. The distance of the weight from the center line of the boat is crucial for calculating the balance.

Here's the plan:
1. We'll consider the torque generated by the remaining engine. Torque is the force applied times the distance from the pivot point (center line of the boat).
2. Then, we'll calculate the weight needed on the other side of the boat, at an 18-inch distance from the center, to produce an equal torque for balance.

Let's do the math:

- Engine weight: 3000 pounds
- Distance from the center: 36 inches
- Torque = Weight × Distance from center

We need to find the weight (W) required at 18 inches to balance this torque. The equation will be:

\[ Torque_{engine} = Torque_{balance} \]
\[ 3000 \text{ lbs} \times 36 \text{ inches} = W \times 18 \text{ inches} \]

Let's calculate W.

### Detailed Elaboration on Mass Balance Certification for US RNG Exports to the EU

#### 1. **Sustainability Verification**

##### **Certification Requirements**

**Objective**: To ensure that RNG imported into the EU meets stringent sustainability standards similar to those applied within the EU.

1. **Sustainability Criteria**:
   - **Greenhouse Gas Emission Savings**: RNG must achieve significant greenhouse gas emission reductions compared to fossil fuels. The EU's Renewable Energy Directive (RED II) stipulates that biofuels must provide at least a 65% GHG savings for new installations starting from 2021  .
   - **Land Use and Biodiversity**: RNG production must comply with criteria that protect land use and biodiversity, ensuring that feedstock cultivation does not adversely impact high biodiversity areas or high carbon stock lands .

2. **Recognized Certification Schemes**:
   - **ISCC (International Sustainability and Carbon Certification)**: One of the widely recognized schemes for certifying biofuels, including RNG, ensuring compliance with EU sustainability criteria.
   - **REDcert**: Another certification scheme recognized by the EU, designed to meet the requirements of RED II. Both ISCC and REDcert involve detailed audits and compliance checks to verify sustainability throughout the supply chain  .

##### **Traceability and Documentation**

**Objective**: To ensure that the renewable attributes of RNG are maintained and verifiable from production to end-use.

1. **Chain of Custody**:
   - **Mass Balance Methodology**: This involves tracking the volume of RNG produced and ensuring that an equivalent volume is accounted for throughout the supply chain. The mass balance approach allows for mixing with conventional natural gas while ensuring that the total amount of renewable gas injected into the grid is equivalent to the amount certified and sold  .
   - **Certification Bodies**: Certified bodies conduct regular audits and inspections to ensure compliance with the mass balance approach. This includes checking production records, supply chain documentation, and verifying that the amount of RNG sold as renewable matches the amount produced and injected into the grid .

2. **Guarantees of Origin (GoO)**:
   - **Issuance and Use**: Guarantees of Origin are issued to certify that a certain amount of gas has been produced from renewable sources. These certificates can be traded independently of the physical gas, allowing flexibility in the market  .
   - **Documentation**: GoO documentation must clearly state the source, volume, and sustainability credentials of the RNG, ensuring transparency and trust in the renewable attributes of the gas imported into the EU【10†source】.

metadata.text:
California RNG market

California is one of the leading states with higher adoption of renewable natural gas (RNG) friendly policies warranting around 12 Million MMBTU/yr of RNG potential.
So far 13 million cumulative CA LCFS credits and 0.3 billion RINs in 2022 has been generated in California
The adoption of RNG will be successful if incentives from various programs are sustained for several years which will give private developers the confidence of return.
California remains the nation’s leader in the creation of cutting-edge programs to reduce dangerous GHG emissions. The legislature enacted Senate Bill 32 in 2016 mandating the California Air Resources Board (CARB) to cut statewide emissions by at least 40% below 1990 levels by 2030. Natural gas is a key source of the GHG emissions which is the focus of these laws; present consumption exceeds 2 trillion cubic feet (tcf) per year for electricity generation industrial applications space and water heating and transportation.








California has been one of the major states which has up taken the RNG production. RNG is a common fuel for heavy vehicles and medium-duty work fleets. It has been effective in reducing carbon emissions from transport fuels in the state. Californian agencies have implemented policies to encourage the development of RNG that can eventually replace fossil natural gas fuel while using the same transportation and fueling infrastructure as today’s fossil natural gas. However due to technical challenges RNG supplies within California are limited compared with Texas which has the highest active production capacity and other states such as Pennsylvania and Ohio

Due to the limited domestic supply California depends on the supply of RNG from outside states where book and claim accounting for RNG has been accelerating the demand. However this scenario might change in the coming years with a high number of RNG plants in the planned status in the state. I

Key targets include reducing methane by 40% hydrofluorocarbon gases by 40% and anthropogenic black carbon by 50% below 2013 levels by 2030; developing strategies and incentives to increase renewable gas production and use; reducing organics landfill disposal; and focusing on dairy and livestock sector methane to help achieve reduction goals


RNG consumption

In 2023 Q1 California consumed around 45 million diesel gallon equivalents of RNG accounting for more than 1.06M credits which constitute 15.86% of total credits generated. Moreover the cumulative credits from RNG are close to 13 million. Majority of these credits come from dairy Biogas plants


The uptake of clean fuels including RNG has been significant in recent years. Percentage wise credits generated from Bio-CNG credits are close to 15.86% in 2023 Q1. There has been an increasing trend in the last few years. This increase is largely attributed to book and claim mechanism which is applicable to RNG in California. From our interaction with the market participants and from market news it is evident that so far the LCFS credit prices (low as $66.15 per ton ) has been successful to provide developers with a financial return on the RNG project. This has led to injection of RNG into California’s natural gas transportation fuel network from Los Angeles San Diego Irvine Sacramento and Livermore. Local and state landfill tipping fee laws will be critical to the successful use of RNG from municipal solid waste for transportation purposes. Higher tipping costs in addition to LCFS credits will improve incentives to manufacture RNG from municipal solid waste.








Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS):
The RFS specifies the amount of biofuel that must be incorporated into transportation fuel each year from 2006 to 2023. The program was created as part of the Energy Policy Act 2005 and was revised by the 2007 Energy Independence and Security Act. There are four nested categories in the program: renewable biofuels advanced biofuels biomass-based diesel and cellulosic biofuels. 
Each category has its own volume requirement also known as a Renewable Volume Obligation (RVO) as well as a different sort of renewable identification number (RIN). In 2013 EPA categorized RNG as cellulosic biofuels that receive the market’s highest value RINs D3 RINs. 
In 2022 out of the total 21 billion RINS generated through RFS around 0.65 billion RINS were generated in the D3 category. 
RIN generation from RNG and RLG

Interesting that there seems to be an existing market for renewable LNG




The prices for D3 RINs has been always higher than other types of RIN. Although RFS has been a major policy at the federal level it has impacted the uptake of renewable fuel volumes in California as well. It is estimated that around 20% of renewable fuel volumes under RFS has been consumed in California of which approximately 5% is RNG. This amounts to 0.3 Billion RINS from RNG in 2022.

RIN pricing (Rin D3 always highest pricing)




Renewable natural gas (RNG) use as a transportation fuel has increased in California and in 2021 alone RNG use resulted in the displacement of 2.78 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e). This is similar to removing 600145 gasoline powered cars off California roadways for one year.
This proves that biomethane sourced from dairy digesters local landfills wastewater treatment plants commercial food waste facilities and agricultural operations provides the most affordable and proven solution to decarbonize medium- and heavy-duty transportation today.












































The Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) 
Is an emissions trading rule designed to reduce the average carbon intensity of transportation fuels vs convention fossil fuels. 
The California Air Resources Board identified the Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) as one of the nine discrete early action measures to reduce California's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions that cause climate change. The LCFS is a key part of a comprehensive set of programs in California to cut GHG emissions and other smog-forming and toxic air pollutants by improving vehicle technology reducing fuel consumption and increasing transportation mobility options. The LCFS is designed to decrease the carbon intensity of California's transportation fuel pool and provide an increasing range of low-carbon and renewable alternatives which reduce petroleum dependency and achieve air quality benefits.

Other jurisdictions are joining California which is evident in the Pacific Coast Collaborative a regional agreement between California Oregon Washington and British Columbia to strategically align policies to reduce GHG and promote clean energy. CARB has been routinely working with these jurisdictions and over time these LCFS programs will build an integrated West Coast market for low-carbon fuels that will create greater market pull increased confidence for investors of low carbon alternative fuels and synergistic implementation and enforcement programs. CARB also continues to engage with representatives from Canada and Brazil as they develop similar clean fuels program.


How is LCFS calculated? 
One LCFS credit is equal to one metric ton (1MT CO2) of avoided GHG emissions and is a function of the: Difference in CI between the baseline fuel (gasoline/diesel) and alternative fuel. Volume of baseline fuel displaced.

How is the LCFS credit price set?
The credit-based mechanism allows the marketplace to determine the fuel mix in California and the regulation sets the target or CI intensity limit. Market actors can then choose how to comply by adopting low carbon fuels or purchasing credits to achieve compliance.
Given that the market sets the price of credits based on how many are in circulation at a given time prices can be volatile. The exhibit below depicts the market price volatility since LCFS was enacted in 2013. To limit the impact of LCFS credit prices on end users California Air Board  put a $200 cap on credit prices in 2016 dollars adjusted for inflation annually. The cap was $253.53 in 2023.

How does LCFS deficits interact with fuel prices?
Designed as a cross-subsidy program obligated parties under LCFS who do not meet CI targets generate deficits and can meet the program requirements by buying credits from producers of low carbon fuel. For instance in 2021 the average CI of crude oil supplied to California refineries was 12.88 gCO2e/MJ nearly 9 percent higher than the target CI of 11.78 gCO2/MJ set by the LCFS program. Obligated parties who produced or imported that crude had to purchase credits to offset the deficit.
While there are several steps involved in transforming crude oil into retail fuel which could affect its CI if we assume retail fuel has the same CI undercompliance (9%) as crude oil from the 2021 example and given that LCFS credits were $200 at that time it would amount to a ~23 cent/gal compliance cost for the party who owns and dispenses that fuel. Conversely in 2023 LCFS credits were trading below $100 but CI compliance data is not available preventing a similar calculation. Regardless because retail prices for fuel for the everyday consumer depend on a series of variables  there is not a direct correlation between the LCFS compliance cost and consumer prices.






Case Study: The LCFS program can support EV supply equipment service providers and can add an additional source of revenue
To understand how EV fueling earns LCFS credits let’s take the example of charging a Chevy Bolt EV for which the alternative clean energy fuel is electricity and the baseline fuel is gasoline.
In California the cost of electricity from the grid averages 20 to 30 cents per kWh. EV fueling at public charging stations increases the amount consumers must pay as EVSPs must pay for the additional costs of charging hardware site costs software operation maintenance and more. Today public chargers often have relatively low utilization. Until more EVs are on the street cost recovery can be uncertain for EV charging providers and varies considerably depending on the utility rate structure.
Incentives such as those provided by LCFS can significantly improve the business case for public charging and lower public charging costs for EV drivers. Using the CARB LCFS calculator and assuming the maximum LCFS credit price of $200 per credit fully charging a 65kWh Chevy Bolt battery would earn $10.25 in LCFS credits or approximately 16 cents per kWh which would offset 50–80 percent of the electricity cost.
At the time of this analysis the average LCFS credit price was $74 per credit which would translate to LCFS revenue of 6 cents per kWh of EV fueling only covering 20–30 percent of the electricity cost — a 62 percent drop from the maximum possible incentive. Thus the price volatility of LCFS credits can significantly impact cost recovery and EVSP business models.
Impact on electric fleets
LCFS can help build the business case for commercial vehicle owners of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles to electrify. Electric fleet operators may choose to own the charging stations and claim LCFS credits or partner with EVSPs to share LCFS revenue via charging discounts or other contractual agreements. As a result LCFS can help lower the total cost of ownership (TCO) by lowering fueling costs which can help justify the higher upfront vehicle cost.
Sources of LCFS credits
Now that we have understood how crucial LCFS is to strengthening public and fleet EV charging infrastructure let’s take a closer look at the sources for LCFS credits. The exhibit below shows LCFS credits generated from 2011 to Q3 2022 by fuel type.



The volume of credits generated is increasing flooding the LCFS marketplace which drives credit values lower. Electricity as a transportation fuel currently generates the smallest share of LCFS credits while the lions’ share of LCFS credits — nearly three quarters — is being directed to biomass-based fuels. Several stakeholders including National Resources Defense Council (NRDC) have highlighted concerns over potential unintended consequences such as over-incentivizing the production of livestock biomethane and crop-based biofuels and diverting resources away from the ZEV transition.
Fueling credits are based on the CI of the fuel: the lower the CI the more credit it earns. The accounting of CI for biomethane and crop-based fuels is a particular concern as the CI of fuels from dairy and crop feedstocks are reported to be lower due to inaccurate accounting of their impact. NRDC has also proposed measures to improve the effectiveness of the LCFS program by redirecting credits away from biofuels. These biofuels also earn additional revenue through the federal Renewable Fuel Standards program which does not include electricity for EV charging in its scope. In summary the current credit generation mechanism presents a relative disadvantage for electricity a cleaner transportation fuel that needs greater incentive support for a zero-emission future.
The significance of LCFS
LCFS is a landmark piece of legislation which created for the first time a market-based mechanism to slash transportation emissions by working on four sectors of the economy: energy environment agriculture and transportation. The additional revenue provided by LCFS credits funded by higher emission fuels incentivizes the market to move to cleaner fuels such as electricity.
One could say that LCFS has contributed to California’s high EV adoption. While there has been significant critique of its support of bio-fuels instead of zero-emissions transportation the LCFS model has led policymakers to even consider introducing a LCFS like regulation at a federal level.Image Format: Portable Network Graphic (PNG)
